Go to the abode of Śiva, O Gaṅgā; go to the abode of Brahmā, O Sarasvatī! (65)
Let the virtuous Kamalālayā remain here in my house;
for he whose wife is easy to manage, virtuous, and devoted to her husband, [is truly blessed]. 66.
In this world he finds happiness in heaven, and in the next world he attains dharma and liberation;
he whose wife is devoted to her husband is liberated, pure, and happy.
He is as good as dead while living, impure, miserable, and indeed possesses a wife of ill character. || 67 ||
Thus ends the sixth chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 6 ||
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter seven.
Now begins the seventh chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Having spoken thus, O Nārada, the Lord of the worlds ceased speaking;
the goddesses, embracing one another, wept most bitterly.
Trembling, with eyes filled with tears from both grief and fear, they spoke in turn to that Lord.
Having observed them all, Sarasvatī said:
"O Lord, grant us release from the curse; the sorrow of our entire lives has been witnessed."
Abandoned by their husbands while they were still alive, how could those women survive?
"I shall certainly renounce my body through yoga in Bhārata;
for one who has transgressed [the rules] must surely and inevitably fall. (4)
Gangā said: "O Lord of the World, by what offense have I been abandoned by you?
I shall give up my life; let me incur the death penalty for being innocent. (5)
That man on earth who abandons a faultless beloved goes to a terrible hell, even if he were the Lord of All.
Padmā said:
"O Lord, you are the very embodiment of goodness; how then can there be anger in you? O Master, please show favor toward your two wives; forgiveness is the highest virtue. (7)
Due to the curse of Bhāratī, I shall indeed descend into Bhārata with a portion of myself;
for how long will my stay there last, and when shall I behold your feet? (8)
Sinners will transfer their sin immediately through immersion and bathing;
by what means shall I be liberated from that, so that I may come to your abode? (9)
"O Acyuta, when shall I, as the virtuous daughter of Dharmadhvaja, having assumed the form of Tulasī through a portion [of your power], attain your lotus feet?"
"I shall become a tree-form, the presiding deity of you;
O ocean of compassion, tell me when you will deliver me. (11)
If the Gaṅgā shall go to Bhārata due to the curse of Sarasvatī, when will she, freed from that curse and from sin, attain you? (12)
If the Goddess of Speech should go to Bhārata due to the curse of Gaṅgā, when will she, having been released from that curse, regain her place with you? (13)
O Lord, you speak of going to that voice, to the abode of Brahmā, to the Gaṅgā, or to the temple of Śiva; therefore, please forgive those words of yours.
Having spoken thus, she washed the feet of the Beloved of Kamalā and bowed down;
then, binding her hair with her own locks, she wept again and again. || 15 ||
"Anxious to bestow grace upon his devotees,
Padmanābha, placing that Padmā upon his own chest, spoke to her with a slight smile playing upon his face."
The Blessed Lord said: "O Goddess of the gods, I shall carry out your word, and I shall also take possession of it; listen, O lotus-eyed one. (16)
"Let one portion of Bhāratī go to the land of Bhārata in the form of a river;
let half of her remain in the abode of Brahmā, and let the other half herself reside in my house. (17)
That Gaṅgā, who was brought by Bhagīratha and will go to the land of Bhārata to purify the three worlds, herself remains in my home. 18.
Right there, she shall obtain the difficult-to-attain crown of Candramauli;
thereafter, even though fallen by her own nature, she shall become exceedingly purified.
"O lovely-eyed one, go to Bhārata by means of a portion of a fraction; there you shall take the form of the river Padmāvatī and the Tulasī tree. (20)
When five thousand years of the Kali age have passed, your liberation shall come;
you rivers, as well as my own abode, you shall enter.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter seven.
For all embodied beings, even calamity is the cause of prosperity;
for without calamity, whose greatness could there be in this world of lotus-born Brahmā? (22)
And for you virtuous ones who worship my mantra, there shall be liberation from sin through bathing and immersion, as well as through seeing and touching me. (23)
O beautiful one, whatever innumerable holy places exist upon the earth shall become purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. 24.
The devotees who worship my mantra rest in Bhārata in order to purify and redeem this most sacred earth. (25)
Wherever my devotees reside and wash their feet, that place shall certainly become a great sacred site (tīrtha) and supremely pure. ||26||

The killer of a woman, the killer of a cow, the ungrateful, the killer of a Brahmin, and the violator of the guru’s bed—become purified and liberated while living simply by the touch and sight of my devotee. 27.

One who has neglected the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, one who has omitted the twilight prayers, an atheist, or even a slayer of a man—becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (28)
One who lives by the sword, one who lives by ink, a washerman, a village beggar, or a bullock-driver becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (29)
A betrayer of trust, a slayer of friends, or one who gives false testimony becomes purified by the touch and sight of my devotee, even if he has stolen what was entrusted to him. (30)

Whether one is extremely fierce, a defiler of men, a paramour, the husband of an unchaste woman, or even the son of a low-caste woman, such a person is purified by the touch and sight of my devotee. (31)
Even the cook of Śūdras, Devala, or a village priest who has not been initiated becomes pure by the touch and sight of my devotee. (32)
One’s father, mother, wife, brother, son, daughter, the family of the preceptor, sister, and a kinsman who is blind; ||33||
O beautiful one, he who does not support his mother-in-law and father-in-law is a great sinner; yet he is purified by the touch and sight of my devotee.
Even a Brahmin who destroys an aśvattha tree, one who reviles my devotees, or one who eats the food of a Śūdra, becomes purified by the sight of my devotee. (35)
One who steals the property of the gods, one who misappropriates the property of Brahmins, a seller of lac, iron, and mercury, as well as one who sells his own daughter; || 36 ||
Even those who have committed great sins and those among Śūdras who burn the corpses of others shall become purified by the touch and sight of my devotees. (37)
Śrī Mahālakṣmī said:
O you who are eager to bestow grace upon devotees, tell me the characteristics of those devotees by whose sight and touch even the lowest of men are instantly purified. (38)
Devoid of devotion to Hari and possessed of great egoism, they are rogues devoted to self-praise, deceitful, and revilers of the virtuous. (39)
All sacred fords are purified by their bathing and immersion;
by the dust of their feet and by the water from their feet, the earth is sanctified.
For those who desire either the sight or the touch [of them] in Bhārata, the supreme gain for all is the company of Vaiṣṇavas. (41)
For holy fords are not made of water, nor are gods made of clay or stone;
they purify only after a long time, whereas devotees of Viṣṇu purify in an instant—how wonderful!
Sūta said:
Having heard the words of Mahālakṣmī, the beloved of Lakṣmī, smiling, began to explain the supreme, hidden truth. 43.
The Blessed Lord said: O Lakṣmī, the characteristics of devotees are hidden in the Śrutis and Purāṇas;
they are meritorious in nature, destroyers of sin, bestowers of happiness, and granters of both worldly enjoyment and liberation. 44.
That which is essential and must be guarded should not be spoken to the wicked;
I tell you, who are pure and as dear to me as my own life—listen! (45)
The Vedas declare that the Viṣṇu-mantra which falls upon the ear from the mouth of a guru belongs to that most excellent of men, who is indeed pure.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter 8:
Previously, there were a hundred men; likewise, from the mere fact of their birth—
Whether situated in heaven or in hell, one attains liberation at that very moment. ||47||
By whomsoever birth has been obtained, wherever, or among which beings—those who are liberated while living (jīvanmukta) are purified and go at the time of death to the abode of Hari. 48.
A mortal endowed with devotion to me is liberated and becomes possessed of my qualities;
he whose conduct is dependent on my qualities and who is constantly absorbed in my stories [is likewise freed]. 49.
Merely by hearing of my qualities, he was filled with joy, his hair stood on end, his voice became choked with emotion, his eyes filled with tears, and he was utterly forgetful of himself. (50)
He does not desire happiness, nor the fourfold liberation beginning with *sālokya*, nor even the state of Brahmā or immortality; his only desire is in my service. (51)
He does not desire even in a dream the state of Indra, the state of Manu, or the state of Brahmā—all so difficult to attain—nor the enjoyments of the kingdom of heaven and other such realms. (52)
O devotees, such a birth is very difficult to obtain even while wandering through Bhārata;
those who hear of my qualities are constantly filled with joy by what they hear. 53.
Having purified the earth, they go to Nara, my sacred abode;
thus everything has been told regarding Padma—act as is appropriate.
At her command, they did so; Hari remained seated upon his comfortable throne.
Thus ends the seventh chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 7 ||
Now begins the eighth chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: Sarasvatī came to the holy field in Bhārata.
By the curse of Gaṅgā, she herself remained in a portion within the abode of Hari.
Having gone to Bhārata, Bhāratī and Brāhmī, the beloved of Brahmā, became the presiding deity of speech; for that reason, she is celebrated as Vāṇī.
For Hari is seen everywhere—in lakes, ponds, streams, and rivers; because he is the possessor of these waters (*sarasvān*), this river is therefore named after him, Sarasvatī. (3)
And that river Sarasvatī is a sacred ford (tīrtha) and purifying;
she has the nature of a blazing fire for the burning away of the sins of the wicked. ||4||
Afterwards, O Nārada, the Bhagirathi was brought to the earth by Bhagīratha;
he indeed went there by means of a portion [of himself] due to the curse of Vāṇī.
At that very moment, the omnipresent Śiva held her upon his head;
he was able to endure her force only through the prayer of the Earth.
Padmā departed with a portion [of herself], and she became the river Padmāvatī;
while another portion remained herself in the abode of Hari in Bhārata due to the curse of Bhāratī.
Then another [portion] of her, through a fraction of her power, took birth in Bhārata;
she was known as Lakṣmī, the daughter of Dharmadhvaja, and also as Tulasī.
Due to the curse of Hari, she, the purifier of the universe, became a tree by means of a portion of her being. ||9||
Having remained in Bhārata for five thousand years, both before the curse of Sarasvatī and after the onset of Kali,
they abandoned their river-forms and departed for the abode of Śrī Hari.
All those holy places that exist, excluding Kāśī and Vṛndāvana,
shall go to Vaikuṇṭha along with them by the command of Hari.
Śālagrāma, Śakti-Śiva, and Jagannātha, having abandoned Bhārata at the end of ten thousand years of the Kali age, go to their own abode. (12)
The virtuous ones, the ancient conch shells used for the ancestral libations (śrāddha),
and the rites prescribed in the Vedas likewise departed together with them.
The chanting of his fame and virtues,
as well as the Vedāṅgas and the Śāstras, went along with them.
They went together with them to the worship of the gods, the invocation of the gods' names, the village deities, as well as to religious observances, austerities, and fasting.
The virtuous, the true Dharma, and the Vedas—all shall become devoted to wicked conduct, joined with falsehood and deceit;
thereafter, worship devoid of Tulasī shall prevail. (16)
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter eight.
Thereafter, all people will become deceitful, cruel, hypocritical, possessed of great egoism, thieves, and harmful. (17)
Thereafter, the distinction between male and female, the distinction between women, marriage, and even the distinction between property and its owner will exist without fear. (18)
All men are under the sway of women, and in every house there are unchaste women who constantly strike their husbands with threats and reproaches.
The mistress of the house and the housewife are both inferior due to their lack of prosperity;
likewise, the mother-in-law and the father-in-law are equal to a maidservant and a slave for the daughter-in-law.
In his home, the powerful kinsmen related by birth and those related by learning do not even engage in conversation;
likewise, people remain strangers to him, as do his own male relatives.
Men are incapable of performing any action without the command of women. 22.
The Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras will be devoid of their proper castes and conduct;
their twilight devotions and sacred threads will undoubtedly be lost. (23)
The four castes will indeed adopt the conduct of barbarians;
they will abandon their own scriptures and study the treatises of barbarians. (24)
In the Kali age, the lineages of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas shall become servants of Śūdras;
they will all become cooks, washermen, and ox-drivers.
All people are devoid of truth, the earth is devoid of crops, trees are devoid of fruit, and women are devoid of offspring. ||26||
Likewise, cows devoid of milk, milk from which butter has been extracted, a husband and wife lacking affection, and householders who have abandoned truth; ||27||
The kings were bereft of majesty, and the subjects were oppressed by taxes;
the great rivers, the ponds, the caves, and other such places were devoid of water.
Deprived of dharma and devoid of merit, even the four castes themselves remain so;
beyond that, not a single person possessing merit remains among hundreds of thousands.
Men, women, and children will become contemptible and deformed in appearance; thereafter, there will be evil rumors and loathsome sounds. (30)
Some villages and cities were devoid of people and terrifying; some were occupied by only a few huts and a single person. (31)
The forests will become like villages and towns,
and all people living in the forests will be oppressed by taxes.
Crops will grow even in ponds and rivers;
in the Kali age, those born of noble lineages will become degraded.
O Nārada, those who speak falsely, the deceitful, the crafty, and the untruthful shall exist; and even the most excellent fields shall be devoid of crops.
The lowly and the eminent, the wealthy and those devoted to the gods, the atheists, the violent and the merciless, the citizens and the murderers of men—[all these were there]. (35)
In the Kali age, men and women everywhere will be dwarfish, afflicted by diseases, short-lived, plagued by ailments, and devoid of youth. (36)
At sixteen years of age, women have grey hair; at twenty, they are very old.
An eight-year-old girl is a young woman, yet she may be menstruating and even pregnant. A woman who has given birth at the end of a year is already possessed of old age at sixteen.
In the Kali age, every woman who has sons is to be slain.
All four castes who sell their daughters, those who have sexual intercourse with their mother, their wife, or their daughter-in-law, those who eat food provided by such adulterers,
and those who live off the food of men who violate their daughters or sisters— [these are all outcastes]. (39)
In the Kali age, there will arise those who sell the names of Hari.
Having himself bestowed gifts for the sake of increasing his fame,
he will subsequently transgress his own gift.
He will transgress everything— the way of the gods, the way of Brahman, the way of the teacher’s household, and whatever has been given, whether by himself or by another.
Some were violators of virgins, some were violators of mothers-in-law, some were violators of daughters-in-law, and some indeed were violators of all women.
In the Kali age, there will be some who go to their sisters, those who go to their co-wives and mothers, and those who go to the wives of their brothers.

In every household, they will indeed commit acts of approaching women who should not be approached. Thus ends the eighth chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Śrīmad Devībhāgavatamahāpurāṇa. [Page 591]
Having abandoned the womb of their mothers, they will wander everywhere.
In the Kali age, there is no final determination regarding wives and husbands, nor concerning offspring, villages, and especially material possessions. (46)
All were speakers of falsehood, all were thieves and libertines;
they were mutual destroyers and all were murderers of men. (47)
The lineages of the Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas will become sinful;
they will engage in the trade of lac, metals, juices, and salt.
Those of the Brahmin lineage who ride bulls, those who burn the corpses of Śūdras, all those who eat the food of Śūdras, and all those who take pleasure with Śūdra women [shall fall]. 49.

Those who have abandoned the five great sacrifices, those who eat on the new-moon night (Kuhū-rātri), those who are devoid of the sacred thread, and those who are devoid of the twilight prayers and ritual purity; || 50 ||
A wanton woman, a usurer, a procuress, and one in her menses shall become a cook in the kitchens of Brahmins. (51)
In the Kali age, there is no restriction regarding foods, nor particularly regarding wombs; all people of the various stages of life and castes are considered Mlecchas. 52.
Thus, when the Kali age has fully set in, everything will consist of barbarians;
trees will be only a cubit in height, and humans will be no larger than a thumb.
The son of the brahmin Viṣṇuyaśas will be Kalki;
he is a portion of a fraction of Nārāyaṇa, a lord, and the best among the strong.
With his long sword and riding upon a long-necked steed,
he will, within three nights, rid the earth of the Mlecchas.
Having made the earth devoid of foreigners, he will cause himself to vanish;
and the earth, being without a king, will become overrun by bandits.
For six nights, the earth will be drenched by rainfalls as thick as pillars;
the world will become empty of trees, empty of houses, and empty of people.
Then, O sage, the twelve Ādityas will rise;
by their splendor, the earth shall reach a state of parched dryness. (58)
When the invincible Kali age has passed and the Kṛta age has begun,
Dharma, endowed with austerity and purity, will become complete.
On this earth, there were ascetic and most righteous Brahmins who were knowers of the Vedas,
and in every household, there were women who were devoted to their husbands and most virtuous.
All the kings were Kṣatriyas, devoted to the Brahmins, high-minded,
majestic, most righteous, and always engaged in meritorious deeds.
The Vaiśyas were devoted to trade, devoted to the Brahmins, and righteous;
and the Śūdras were of virtuous character, most pious, and servants of the Brahmins.
The lineages of the Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas were all devoted to the Goddess;
they were all intent upon the mantras of the Goddess and dedicated to the meditation on the Goddess.

In the Kṛta Yuga, men who were knowers of the Śruti, Smṛti, and Purāṇas approached their wives only during the proper season; indeed, there was not even a trace of unrighteousness, for dharma was complete.
In the Tretā age, Dharma stands on three feet; in the Dvāpara, it then stands on two;
when the Kali age has occurred, it stands on one foot, and after that, there is the total disappearance of all.
Likewise, O Brahmin, seven days (vāras) and sixteen lunar days (tithis) are recorded;
similarly, there are twelve months and six seasons. ||66||
The two fortnights and the two solstices; a day consists of four watches, and the night likewise consists of four watches; a month is composed of thirty such days. (67)
The year is to be known as fivefold according to the sequence of the rules for the calculation of time;
and just as they come and go, so too does the cycle of the four ages (yuga-catuṣṭaya).
When the years of men and the days and nights of the gods are both complete—three hundred and sixty-six years for men being one *yuga* for the gods. (69)
The duration of a divine yuga is known by those who understand the calculation of time;
seventy-one such divine yugas constitute a Manvantara. (70)
The lifespan of the Lord of Śacī should be known as equal to a Manvantara;
and when twenty-eight Indras have passed, one day and night of Brahmā elapses.
When one hundred and eight years have passed, there occurs the fall of Brahmā;
that should be known as the elemental dissolution (prākṛta-pralaya), wherein the earth is no longer perceived.
In the glorious Śrīmad Devībhāgavatamahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, this is the chapter.
All things submerged in water—Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest, as well as all the wise sages—are dissolved into the Truth, the conscious Self. 73.
In that very state, primordial nature (prakṛti) is dissolved; therein lies the dissolution of nature.
O Sage, when this natural dissolution has occurred and Brahmā has fallen [into sleep], [the world remains].
O Sage, it is said that even a moment’s time of the Śrī Devī [is immeasurable];
in this way, all entire universes perish.
And within the interval of a single blink of an eye, through the process of creation once again—how many kinds of creation are there, or how many kinds of dissolution as well? (76)
O Nārada, what man knows the number of the kalpas that have passed and gone, as well as the creations, the dissolutions, and the cosmic eggs?
What man can know the number of Brahmās and others within the cosmic egg?
He alone is the Lord of all the cosmic eggs.
The Supreme Self of all bears the form of existence, consciousness, and bliss;
Brahmā and the others are His portions, and the Great Virāṭ is a portion of Him.
And his portion was the Virāṭ, the subtle; she herself is this supreme Prakṛti. From her presence, Ardhanārīśvara was likewise born.
That very Kṛṣṇa became twofold, both two-armed and four-armed;
the four-armed one is in Vaikuṇṭha, while he himself is two-armed in Goloka.
Everything from Brahmā down to a blade of grass is composed of primordial nature (prakṛti);
whatever is created from primordial nature is entirely perishable.
Such is the cause of creation—the Truth, eternal, and ancient;
the Supreme Brahman, consisting of its own will, devoid of qualities, and beyond primordial nature (prakṛti).
Free from limiting adjuncts and formless, yet eager to bestow grace upon devotees,
He is that by whose knowledge Brahmā— the lotus-born— creates the cosmic egg.
He is Śiva, the conqueror of death, the destroyer, and the knower of all principles;
through his knowledge and his austerity, he is the Lord of All and possesses great ascetic power. 85.
Endowed with great majesty, he is omniscient and all-seeing;
he is all-pervading, the protector of all, and the bestower of all perfections.
By devotion to whom and by service to whom Viṣṇu, the glorious Lord of all, as well as Mahāmāyā, Prakṛti, the Sovereign consisting of all powers, [are attained]. (87)
She alone is declared to be the Blessed Lady, whose nature is existence, consciousness, and bliss;
through the knowledge of whom, by whose austerity, by whose devotion, and by whose service [all is attained].
Sāvitrī is the mother of the gods and the presiding deity of the Vedas;
she is to be worshipped by the twice-born who know the Vedas, for it is through her service that one gains knowledge of the Veda. (89)
She is the presiding goddess of all sciences, the supreme object of worship for the learned;
through her service and her austerity, she is honored throughout the entire universe. (90)
She is the presiding deity of every village, the bestower of all prosperity, the sovereign of all, worthy of worship by all, and the giver of sons to everyone. ||91||
She is praised by all, omniscient, and the destroyer of all miserable rebirths;
she is born from the left shoulder of Kṛṣṇa and is the presiding deity of Kṛṣṇa’s life-breath.
Through her love and service to the power of Rādhikā, she possesses a life-force superior to Kṛṣṇa’s, as well as a form, good fortune, honor, and dignity that are preeminent above all. (93)
Through her service, she obtained the status of being the wife who resides upon Kṛṣṇa’s chest;
previously, she had performed penance on the mountain Śataśṛṅga.
And for a thousand divine years, solely for the sake of attaining her husband,
she remained until grace was bestowed upon her by Śakti, after which she beheld one who resembled a digit of the moon.
Placing her upon his chest, the all-pervading Lord Kṛṣṇa wept out of compassion and granted her a supreme boon, the most difficult of all to obtain.
Dwell upon my chest as my eternal devotee,
endowed with good fortune, honor, love, and dignity.
"You are my most excellent and eldest, the dearest of all women;
you are the most distinguished and most venerable, and have been praised and honored by me. (98)
"O beloved of my life, this [man] shall be eternally attainable by you and under your control.
Having spoken thus, the Lord of the World then transformed himself into a woman.
And he made that beloved of his life free from co-wives;
and whatever other goddesses there were, they too were honored through service to Śakti.
In the glorious *Śrīmad-Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa*, in the ninth book, chapter nine:
"O sage, whatever kind of austerity those women performed, they obtained a corresponding fruit."
And having performed austerities for a thousand divine years on the Himalayas, [he attained his goal]. (101)
And Durgā, having meditated upon that state, became worthy of worship by all.
Sarasvatī, having performed austerities on Mount Gandhamādana, [attained her goal]. || 102 ||
Having performed penance at Puṣkara for a hundred divine yugas, that Lakṣmī became worthy of veneration by all for a hundred thousand divine years.
By serving the Goddess, she became the bestower of all prosperity;
having performed austerities at Malaya, that Sāvitrī became worthy of worship and salutation. 104.
O Lord, sixty thousand divine years ago, Śaṅkara meditated upon that state for a hundred *manvantaras* while performing penance.
For a hundred intermediate kalpas (manvantaras), Brahmā indeed recited the Śakti-mantra;
for a hundred intermediate kalpas, Viṣṇu, having performed penance, became the protector;
and Śrī Kṛṣṇa, having performed supreme penance for ten intermediate kalpas.
He has reached the divine Goloka and rejoices there even today. 107.
Having performed penance for ten *manvantaras* endowed with devotion,
he indeed became the life-force of all, worthy of worship by all, and the support of all.
Thus, by the penance of the Goddess, all the gods were honored.
Sages, Manus, kings, and Brahmins were likewise honored. || 109 ||
Thus I have related to you everything from the Purāṇa according to tradition, just as it was learned from the mouth of my guru. What more do you wish to hear? 110.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, titled "The Manifestation of Śakti," in the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa within the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Purāṇa.
Now begins the twelfth chapter.
Nārada said:
In the mere twinkling of an eye of the Goddess, there was indeed the fall of Brahmā.
Its falling away is proclaimed as the natural dissolution (prākṛtika-pralaya). || 1 ||
In that [state], during the elemental dissolution (prākṛta-pralaya), the earth is said to be unseen;
all worlds are submerged by water, and everyone is dissolved into the Supreme Self. ||2||
Where did the Earth disappear and where does she reside? And how did she manifest once again at the time of the creation of the universe? (3)
How did that blessed, venerable, all-supporting Jayā come to be?
Tell me her story of birth, which brings about auspiciousness.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: According to the Śruti, the birth of all beings in every initial creation is from the Goddess;
likewise, their manifestation and disappearance occur in all dissolutions.
Listen to the account of the birth of Vasudhā, which is the cause of all auspiciousness,
the destroyer of obstacles, the eradicator of sins, and the increaser of merit.
"Aha! Some say that the earth became blessed by the fat of Madhu and Kaiṭabha; hear now what contradicts that. (7)

That Creator also brings about creation through knowledge in due order;

That [portion] becomes three parts in the Tretā age, two parts in the Dvāpara, and one part in the Kali age; and previously, it was successively reduced to a fraction of that.
When but a single digit of the Kali age remains, it is like the crescent of the moon on the new-moon night;
just as the splendor of the sun in summer is not such again in winter.
As it is at midday during the day, so it is not at evening or morning; by the power of time, it gradually rises and then proceeds toward its state of infancy. (49)
After reaching its peak, it subsequently sets once more;
during the day it moves in concealment, but by time, it becomes hidden in the thick clouds of a stormy day.
When seized by Rāhu, the moon trembles, yet it becomes clear once more and arises fully complete on the night of the full moon. || 51 ||
Such a person does not remain constant; day by day they go to ruin, yet they recover their vigor again, becoming increasingly enraged day after day.
Endowed with prosperity during the bright fortnight, he becomes withered by consumption during the dark fortnight;
on a day eclipsed by Rāhu, he is withered, and on a cloudy day, he does not shine.
In due time, the moon will become white [waning], its splendor lost through the change of time;
and Bali will become Indra, his splendor lost now in Sutala.
In due time, the earth—the supporter of all, the bearer of wealth—became rich with crops;
then, in due time, submerged in water and flooded by the waters, it vanished.
All things perish in time and indeed arise from time;
both the moving and the unmoving perish and come forth by means of time. (56)
The equality of the Lord, of Brahman, the Supreme Self,
is such that I am the conqueror of death because of the dissolution of the countless material world.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter twenty-one.
And I shall behold him again and again, time after time;
he is both the form of primordial nature (prakṛti) and is remembered as that very Puruṣa. || 58 ||
He is both the Self and the individual soul, the Supreme who assumes manifold forms;
he indeed constantly performs the chanting of His names and qualities. (59)
In due time, he conquers death, the fear of birth and disease, and old age;
by him Vidhi was made the creator, and Viṣṇu was made the protector.
O King, having appointed Kālāgnirudra for the purpose of destruction, we—who were once characterized by ego—were made objects of his domain. 61.
I constantly perform the chanting of his name and qualities;
by that, I have become a conqueror of death and am fearless through this knowledge.
"He flees from the fear of death as one does from the fear of Death itself, just as serpents flee from Vainateya," having said this,
that Lord of All became intent upon Him with his whole being.
And Śambhu ceased speaking in the midst of the assembly, O Nārada;
and the king, having heard those words, praised them again and again.
Śaṅkhacūḍa spoke sweetly to the God with supreme humility:
"O Lord, that which has been spoken by you is not remembered as anything other than true. (65)
Nevertheless, listen to my report regarding a certain truth:
you have just now stated that there is great sin in betraying one's kinsmen. (66)
Having seized all his possessions, why was Bali sent away?
O Lord, I have taken away all his supreme sovereignty.
Even Gadādhara was not able to extract him from the earthen image;
how then was Hiraṇyākṣa, along with his brother, slain by the gods? (68)
And how were the asuras, such as Śumbha and others, struck down by the gods?
Formerly, during the churning of the ocean, the nectar was consumed by the deities. (69)
In this matter, we are the sharers of the afflictions while they enjoy the fruits;
this entire universe is but a plaything of Prakṛti and the Supreme Self.
To whomever and wherever he grants it, to that person shall belong sovereignty; at that time, there will be a perpetual and constant conflict between the gods and the dānavas. (71)
Their defeat is our victory, occurring in due course over time;
therefore, in the event of a conflict between us at that time, any further departure would be utterly fruitless.
This is a great shame for you, a kinsman and relative by marriage of the high-souled Lord, that you now engage in battle with us. (73)
"Victory brings greater fame, while defeat results in loss"—having heard these words, the three-eyed Lord laughed. (74)
Mahādeva spoke an appropriate reply to that lord of the Dānavas:
"In battle with you, who are born of the lineage of Brahmā, [I shall engage]... (75)
O King, what great shame or infamy is there in defeat?
For Hari’s delight was indeed in battle with Madhu and Kaiṭabha. (76)
O King, there was also the battle with Hiraṇyakaśipu along with that very self [of Viṣṇu],
and again the battle with Hiraṇyākṣa by that wielder of the mace.
In the past, a battle was also fought by me against the Tripuras;
it took place with Prakṛti, the sovereign of all and mother of all.
Formerly, there was a most wonderful battle with Śumbha and the others;
you are the foremost devotee at the feet of Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Soul. (79)
"O Hataśva, whichever Daityas have been slain by you, none at all are equal to you. O King, what great shame is there for me in fighting with you? (80)
"Sent in secret by Hari, the refuge of the gods, my firm resolve is this: 'Grant the kingdom to the gods. (81)
"Either engage in battle with me, or what is the purpose of this waste of words?"
Having spoken thus, O Nārada, Śaṅkara ceased there.
And Śaṅkhacūḍa rose up quickly along with his ministers.
Thus ends the twenty-first chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 21 ||
Now begins the twenty-second chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having bowed his head to Śiva, the powerful lord of the Dānavas [spoke].
And he, together with his ministers, quickly ascended the vehicle. ||1||
Śiva swiftly urged forth his own army and the gods;
and the lord of the Dānavas, together with his army, stood ready at the commencement of the battle. ||2||
Mahendra himself fought together with Vṛṣaparvan,
and Bhāskara quickly fought with Vipracitti.
Candra engaged in a supreme battle with Dambha;
Kāla fought with Kālasvara, and Hutāśana with Gokarṇa.
Kubera was [fought] by Kālakeya, Viśvakarman by Maya,
Mṛtyu by Bhayaṅkara, and likewise Yama by Saṃhāra.
Samīraṇa [was pleased] by Vikaṅkaṇa, Varuṇa by Cañcala, Budha by Ghṛtapṛṣṭha, and Śanaiścara by Raktākṣa. ||6||
Jayanta [was born] from Ratnasāra; the Vasus from the hosts of splendors (varcas);
the Aśvins from Dīptimant; Nalakūbara from Dhūmra;
Dharma from Dhuraṃdhara; and Maṅgala from Uṣākṣa.
Indeed, Bhānu [was surpassed] by Śobhākara, and Manmatha by Piṭhara. ||8||
With the Godhāmukha, the Cūrṇana, the Khaḍga, and the Dhvaja;
with the Kāñcīmukha, the Piṇḍa, and the Dhūmra together with Nandin.
And with Viśvapa and Palāśa, the eleven Ādityas and others fought against the other eleven terrifying Rudras.
Mahāmārī fought with Upacaṇḍa and the others,
while Nandīśvara and all the rest [fought] with the hosts of Dānavas.
They fought in a great battle, terrifying even at the time of universal dissolution;
and Śambhu stood at the foot of the banyan tree with the son of Kālī.
And all the hosts of soldiers fought constantly, O sage,
seated upon beautiful jeweled thrones together with ten million dānavas.
And Śaṅkhacūḍa, adorned with jewel ornaments, took up residence there;
as did those warriors of Śaṅkara who had been defeated by the Dānavas.
All the gods fled, terrified and with their bodies wounded;
then Skanda became enraged and granted fearlessness to the gods.
He increased the strength and the power of his own hosts through his splendor;
thus, he alone fought against the multitudes of the Dānavas.
In battle, she slew a hundred akṣauhiṇīs;
the lotus-eyed Kālī struck down the asuras.
Then, becoming exceedingly enraged, he drank the blood of the Dānavas;
taking ten lakhs of lordly elephants, a hundred lakhs, and even by the crores,
he playfully cast them into his mouth with a single hand.
And a thousand kadamba trees danced in the battle, O sage. ||19||
With their bodies wounded by Skanda’s net of arrows, all the Dānavas, despite their prowess in great battle, fled in terror like frightened horses. ||20||
Vṛṣaparvan, Vipracitti, Dambha, and Vikaṅkaṇa—
all of them fought with Skanda and Vikrama.

Mahāmārī fought on and did not turn her back; yet they became utterly agitated, tormented by Skanda’s spear. They did not flee out of fear, for a rain of flowers fell in heaven upon seeing Skanda’s most fierce and formidable battle.
In the glorious Devī Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter twenty-two: how the natural dissolution brought about the destruction of the Dānavas.
The king, having ascended his celestial chariot, let fall a rain of words.
The king's shower of arrows was like a rain of wealth,
and there arose a most terrible darkness as well as the bursting forth of fire.
All the gods, as well as others such as Nandīśvara and the rest, fled;
Kārttikeya alone remained at the forefront of the battle.
And the king sent forth a rain that was irresistible and terrifying, consisting of mountains, serpents, rocks, and likewise trees. (27)
And by the king’s shower of arrows, the son of Śiva was overwhelmed,
like the sun obscured by a dense mist.
The terrifying one cut Skanda’s bow, which was difficult to wield, and shattered his divine chariot, even severing the chariot-seats. ||29||
He shattered the peacock, which had been worn out by the divine weapon,
with a spear that shone like the sun and was capable of slaying that yakṣa.
For a moment he fell into a swoon, but then he regained consciousness;
taking up that divine bow which had been given by Viṣṇu in the past.
Having mounted a chariot fashioned from the finest essence of jewels,
Kārttika took up weapons and missiles and waged a fierce battle.
The son of Śiva, with divine weapons and in a fit of rage, cut down all the serpents, mountains, trees, and boulders as well. 33.
The powerful one extinguished the fire with a Pārjanya weapon;
he effortlessly cut through Śaṅkhacūḍa’s chariot and bow.
He hurled his armor, his charioteer, and his crown-bright diadem, as well as a white-shining spear, into the chest of the lord of the Dānavas.
Having fallen into a swoon, the king regained consciousness;
he mounted another chariot and quickly seized his bow.
And Bāṇa, the best among masters of illusion, released a net of arrows;
O Nārada, he covered Guha in battle with that web of shafts.
He seized an irresistible spear, radiant as the sun at the time of universal destruction, possessing the form of the crest of the fire of dissolution, and enveloped by the splendor of Viṣṇu.
And in his anger, O Kārttikeya, he hurled it with great velocity;
that spear fell upon his chest like a blazing mass of fire. (39)
The mighty Kārttikeya reached Mūla with his power;
Kālī, taking him upon her lap, led him into the presence of Śiva. 40.
And Śiva, by his power, restored him to life through knowledge as if in sport;
he granted him infinite strength, and the majestic one rose up. 41.
The time arrived for the protection of the Kārtika festival;
the heroes, including Nandīśvara and others, followed her.
All the gods, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kinnaras, as well as numerous musical instruments and hundreds of honey-carriers [were present]. (43)

Having gone to the battlefield, she let out a lion’s roar; by the goddess’s lion’s roar, the Dānavas were shaken, and she again and again let out an inauspicious, loud, boisterous laugh. Seeing this, she drank the honey-wine and danced at the head of the battle.
Ugradaṃṣṭrā, Ugradaṇḍā, Koṭakī, and Papāmadhu;
as well as the hosts of Yoginīs and Ḍākinīs, and the hosts of gods and others. || 46 ||
Seeing Kālī, Śaṅkhacūḍa quickly arrived at the battlefield;
the Dānavas were seized with fear, and the king granted them freedom from fear.
Kālī hurled fire resembling the flames of the fire of universal destruction, but the king effortlessly extinguished it with a rain-cloud weapon (pārjanya). || 48 ||
And she hurled a fierce and great wondrous Vāruṇa weapon,
but the lord of the Dānavas effortlessly cut it down with a Gāndharva weapon.
Kāla hurled the Māheśvara [missile], which resembled a crest of fire;
the king swiftly struck it down with ease using the Vaiṣṇava [missile]. 50.
That goddess discharged the Nārāyaṇa weapon preceded by mantras;
seeing it, the king descended from his chariot and prostrated himself.

That weapon, resembling the crest of the fire of universal dissolution, ascended upwards. Śrīmad-Devībhāgavatamahāpurāṇa, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 23. 63. It went upwards like the flame of the fire of cosmic destruction.
And Śaṅkhacūḍa fell prostrate on the ground before him in devotion like a staff.
She discharged the Brahmāstra with great effort, preceded by the recitation of mantras;
the great king neutralized it with his own Brahmāstra.
Then that goddess discharged a divine weapon accompanied by mantras;
the king, however, extinguished it with a net of his own divine weapons.
The goddess forcefully hurled a spear a yojana in length,
and the king, with a network of divine weapons, shattered it into a hundred pieces.
And the goddess, in her wrath, seized the Pāśupata weapon purified by mantras;
and as she was about to hurl it to obstruct [the enemy], an incorporeal voice spoke.
For the high-souled king, there is no death from the Pāśupata [weapon], as long as the armor of Hari’s mantra remains intact. (57)
"As long as the virtue of chastity exists, and as long as young women remain true, so long shall he have neither old age nor death"—such was the word of Brahmā. (58)
Having heard this, Bhadrakālī did not hurl that weapon;
instead, she swallowed a hundred lakhs of Dānavas with ease, as if yawning.
The terrifying goddess rushed with speed to devour Śaṅkhacūḍa,
but the Dānava warded her off with a very sharp divine weapon.
That goddess likewise hurled a sword resembling the summer sun;
the lord of the Dānavas shattered it into a hundred pieces with a divine weapon.
The Great Goddess went toward him with speed to seize him again;
the illustrious lord of all Siddhas, the lord of the Dānavas, grew in size.
With her fist, the terrifying Kālī, filled with wrath, [struck] him.
She shattered his chariot and killed his charioteer.
She hurled a trident resembling the flame of the fire of universal dissolution,
but Śaṅkhacūḍa caught it with his left hand as if in mere play.
With great fury and speed, the goddess struck him with her fist;
the Daitya then reeled and fell into a swoon. || 65 ||
Regaining consciousness in an instant, the valiant one rose up;
he did not engage in hand-to-hand combat with the goddess, but bowed down before her.
He cut down the goddess's weapon and seized it by his own splendor;
being her devotee and a Vaiṣṇava through devotion to his mother, he did not hurl that weapon at her.
Having seized the Dānava and whirled him around again and again, the goddess Kōpilā, with great velocity, sent him soaring upwards.
The powerful Śaṅkhacūḍa fell down from above with great force;
having fallen, he stood up again after bowing to Bhadrakālī.
Filled with joy, and still unwearied from the great battle, he ascended a most beautiful celestial chariot fashioned from the finest essence of the jewel-king.
And that goddess Bhadrakālī, out of hunger, drank the blood of the Dānavas;
having drunk and eaten, she went into the presence of Śaṅkara.
He related the account of the battle in its proper sequence from beginning to end;
having heard it, Śambhu, the destroyer of the Dānavas, laughed.
O Lord, one hundred thousand of the leaders of monkeys remain in the battle now;
that other portion which was consumed has emerged from the mouth of her who is eating them.
And while he was about to slay the lord of the Dānavas in battle with the Pāśupata weapon, an incorporeal voice spoke: "O King, you shall not be slain.
O Indra among kings, he was a man of great wisdom and possessed of immense strength and prowess.
He did not discharge a weapon at me, but severed my arrow. || 75 ||
Thus ends the twenty-second chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa. || 22 ||
Now begins the twenty-third chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having heard the principle of Śiva, he who was proficient in the knowledge of reality [spoke].
And he himself went to the battle along with his own hosts, O Nārada.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter twenty-three.
Śaṅkhacūḍa, having seen Śiva and descended from his celestial chariot,
prostrated himself upon the ground with his head in supreme devotion like a staff.
Having prostrated before him, he swiftly ascended the celestial chariot;
he quickly donned his armor and took up his formidable bow.
In ancient times, the battle between Śiva and Dānava lasted for a full hundred years;
O Brahmin, neither victory nor defeat occurred between them.
The Blessed One had laid down his weapons, and the Dānava had laid down his weapons;
Śaṅkhacūḍa was seated upon his chariot, and the Bull-bannered Lord was mounted upon his bull.
A hundred of the Dānavas were indeed raised up;
those who had died in battle, the omnipresent Lord Śambhu restored to life.
In the meantime, an elderly brahmin, extremely distressed,
arrived at the battlefield and spoke to the lord of the Dānavas.
The old brahmin said:
"O Indra among kings, give alms now to me, a brahmin;
you are the giver of all prosperity, whatever is desired in my mind. (8)
"To you who are now inactive, aged, and thirsty, I shall speak after seeing you; first, however, make [this] true. 9.
"Om," said the king of kings, his face and eyes serene;
"And I am a man seeking armor," he replied with great guile.
Having heard that, Hari indeed took the divine armor and went toward Tulasī in the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa.
Having gone there, he performed the act of impregnation through his illusory power;
then Śambhu took up Hari’s trident against the Dānava.
Resembling the midday sun of summer or the crest of the fire of universal destruction,
it was difficult to ward off, invincible, unfailing, and a slayer of enemies;
in its brilliance it was equal to the discus (cakra) and contained the essence of all weapons and missiles.
It was another bow, difficult to bear and terrifying for both Śiva and Keśava;
it was a thousand *dhanus* in length and a hundred *hasta*s in width, endowed with life, having the form of Brahmā, eternal in nature, and beyond description. ||14-15||
O Nārada, he who was capable of crushing the entire Brahmāṇḍa by his own sport, having weighed it, cast it upon Śaṅkhacūḍa.
Having cast aside his bow and assumed a yogic posture with his mind, the king meditated with devotion upon the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
Having whirled the trident and brought it down upon the Dānava,
she then reduced him, along with his chariot, to ashes by means of that spinning motion.
The king beheld the youth in a divine form, dressed as a cowherd, with two arms, holding a flute in his hand, and adorned with jewel ornaments. || 19 ||
He ascended a vehicle fashioned from the essence of the finest jewels, surrounded by tens of millions of cowherds; having come from Goloka, he proceeded toward the city.
O sage, having gone there, he bowed his head with devotion at the lotus feet of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in the forest of Vṛndāvana during the rāsa dance.
Seeing Sudāmā, their faces and eyes filled with serenity, the two,
overflowing with intense affection, took him onto their laps.
Then Śūla went toward him with speed and great respect;
by means of the bones of Śaṅkhacūḍa, he indeed became of the Śaṅkha lineage.
In various forms, it is eternally pure for the worship of the gods;
the water from a conch is highly praised and supremely pleasing to the deities.
Even the very essence of the waters of sacred fords is not as pure as Śambhu;
wherever the sound of a conch resounds, there Lakṣmī is firmly established.
He who has bathed with the water from a conch shell has bathed in all sacred fords;
the conch shell is the abode of Hari, and where the conch is, there is Hari.
Prosperity dwells right there, and all inauspiciousness has been driven far away, especially by the sound of the conch shells of women and, in particular, of Śūdras. 27.
When he was angry, Lakṣmī departed from that place to another land;
even Śiva, having slain the Dānava, went to the world of Śiva. || 28 ||
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter 24:
[He was] surrounded by the celestial hosts.
The gods, filled with supreme bliss, returned to their own realm.
Delighted and mounted upon his bull,
the drums resounded in heaven and the Gandharvas and Kinnaras sang;
and a continuous rain of flowers fell upon Śiva.
And the gods, as well as the foremost among the lords of sages and others, praised him.
Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. ||23||
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter.
Nārada said:
The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa indeed performed the act of impregnation.
In what form does she reside within the Tulasī? You should explain that to me.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: And the blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, through Viṣṇu-māyā, took up the armor of Śaṅkhacūḍa during the rites of the gods.
Assuming that form once again, he went to the house of his virtuous wife,
desiring to destroy her devotion to her husband and with the intent to kill Śaṅkhacūḍa.
He sounded a drum near the door of the Tulasī grove and,
with shouts of victory at that gate, awakened Sundarī.
Having heard that, the virtuous woman, filled with supreme joy, gazed with great reverence at the chariot through the window on the royal highway.
Having given wealth to the Brāhmaṇas, he caused auspicious rites to be performed;
he gave wealth to the bards, the mendicants, and those who recited praises.
Descending from the chariot, the Lord went to the residence of the Goddess—
a beautiful and most enchanting palace constructed of priceless jewels.
And seeing her beloved before her, she was filled with joy;
she washed his feet, bowed down to him, and wept.
The lustful woman seated him upon a beautiful jeweled throne and gave him betel leaf, exquisitely scented with camphor and other fragrances.
Today my birth and life have truly become fruitful,
as I behold my lord of my life, who had gone to battle, returned once more to my home.
Smiling, casting side-long glances, filled with desire, and her body marked with horripilation,
she questioned her beloved about the events of the battle in a sweet voice.
Tulasī said:
O Lord, how did your victory come about in battle against the destroyer of countless universes? Tell me that, O treasure-house of compassion. (12)
Having heard Tulasī’s words, the Lord of Kamalā laughed and,
assuming the form of Śaṅkhacūḍa, spoke these nectar-like words to her.
The Blessed Lord said:
"O beloved, our battle lasted for a full year;
and, O lovely one, the destruction of all the Dānavas occurred."
Brahmā himself caused joy for the two of us,
and by the command of Brahmā, the authority over the gods was granted.
"I have gone to my own abode, the world of Śiva;
Śiva has departed," having said this, the Lord of the worlds lay down upon his bed. 16.
O Nārada, there the Lord of Ramā sported together with Rāmā;
that virtuous woman [was drawn] by the intensity of their amorous attraction through the enjoyment of pleasure.
She reflected on everything and said, "Who are you?"
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter 24, Tulasī said: "Who are you? Tell me, O Lord of Māyā; I have been enjoyed by you through your Māyā."
"Since my chastity has been violated, therefore I shall curse you!
Having heard Tulasī's words, Hari, out of fear of the curse, [acted]. (19)
O Brahmin, by his divine play, the goddess beheld before her the eternal God of gods, who possessed a most beautiful and enchanting form. (20)
Dark as a fresh rain-cloud, with eyes like autumn lotuses, possessing the grace of ten million Cupids, and adorned with jewel ornaments. ||21||
Seeing him with a slight smile, a serene countenance, adorned and wearing yellow garments,
that passionate woman was playfully overcome by a swoon of desire.
And having regained consciousness once more, she spoke to him again.
Tulasī said: "O Lord, you have no compassion; you are like a stone."
"My master was killed by you through deceit and the violation of dharma;
for you, O Lord, possess a heart of stone and are devoid of compassion. (24)
Therefore, O Lord, may you now become one whose form is like a stone;
those who speak of you as a virtuous being are indeed deluded, there is no doubt. (25)
"How was my devoted [husband] taken away for the sake of another without any fault of his own?"—afflicted by grief, she wept bitterly and lamented again and again. (26)
Then, seeing her compassion, the Lord of Kamalā, who is an ocean of the essence of compassion, spoke in order to awaken her through reasoned argument: 27.
The Blessed Lord said: "O blessed lady, you have performed penance for my sake in Bhārata for a long time;
and for your sake, Śaṅkhacūḍa also performed penance for a very long time."
Having made you his beloved, he too sported with you at that very moment;
now it is fitting that the fruit of your asceticism be granted to you alone. (29)
Having cast off this body and assumed a divine form, sport with me in Rāma; become like Ramā herself. ||30||
May this body, in the form of a river renowned as the Gaṇḍakī, be pure and bestow great merit upon men in the holy land of Bhārata. (31)
And your mass of hair shall become a sacred tree;
born from your hair, it shall be renowned as Tulasī.
O fair-faced one, among all flowers and leaves in the three worlds for the worship of the gods, Tulasī shall be the most preeminent in form.
In heaven, on earth, in the netherworld, and in Goloka in my presence, become you, O Tulasī, the best of trees and the most beautiful among flowers. (34)
In Goloka, on the banks of the Virajā, in the Rāsa dance, in the forest of Vṛndāvana, at the Bhāṇḍīra tree, in the beautiful Campaka grove, and in the sandalwood forest. ||35||
May your dwelling be right here in this grove of Mādhavī, Ketakī, Kunda, Mallikā, and Mālatī flowers—a merit-bestowing place of holiness. (36)
At the roots of Tulasī trees and in sacred places, it shall become the abode of all holy pilgrimage sites (tīrthas) and the bestower of merit. ||37||
And there, O fair-faced one, is my very own empowerment over all the gods, as well as [the power] for the falling of a *tulasī* leaf [to reach them]. (38)
He who performs an ablution with the water of a *tulasī* leaf has bathed in all sacred fords and is initiated into all sacrifices. (39)
Whatever satisfaction Hari might derive from thousands of jars of nectar, that same satisfaction will surely arise from the offering of a tulasī leaf. (40)
O virtuous woman, that fruit which is obtained by the gift of ten thousand cows is obtained by the gift of a Tulasī leaf during the month of Kārttika. 41.

Having again attained a good womb, she obtains an excellent son. *Śrīmad-Devībhāgavatamahāpurāṇa*, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 30. 651.
And a thousand trees bearing fruit are highly praised. 32.
Or if he gives only the gift of the fruit to a Brāhmaṇa,

He shall dwell in the world of the gods for as long as a hundred manvantaras;

That man who, with devotion, gives land endowed with crops and beautiful to a brahmin in the holy field of Bhārata,
is certainly honored in Vaikuṇṭha for a hundred manvantaras.
Furthermore, having attained a good birth, he shall become a great king of the earth. ||37||
The earth does not abandon him for even a hundred future births;

And for a hundred thousand manvantaras, he is glorified in Vaikuṇṭha.
Furthermore, having obtained a noble birth endowed with a hundred thousand villages, the earth does not abandon him for even a hundred thousand lifetimes.
He who gives on the land of Bhārata a city that has good offspring, is excellent, endowed with ripened crops, and graced with various lotus-pools, trees, fruits,
and creepers, is honored on Kailāsa for a period equal to ten million Indras’ lifespans.
Furthermore, O Indra among kings, having attained a good birth in Bhārata, he shall obtain a million cities; of this there is no doubt. (43)
The earth certainly does not abandon him for ten thousand births;
he shall indeed become endowed with supreme sovereignty upon the surface of the earth. 44.
And he who indeed gives to a twice-born man a hundred cities, a region that is highly prosperous, situated in the middle of the land, and filled with subjects; ||45||
Endowed with ponds and lakes and furnished with various kinds of trees,
he is honored in Vaikuṇṭha for the duration of ten million manvantaras.
Furthermore, having attained a noble birth, he shall become the lord of Jambudvīpa,
endowed with supreme sovereignty on earth just like Śakra.
The earth indeed does not abandon him even for ten million births;
he shall become a great sovereign of kings, living until the end of the kalpa.
He who bestows his entire office upon a twice-born man shall, at the end, undoubtedly obtain a fourfold reward. || 49 ||
Whoever gives the land of Jambūdvīpa to a Brahmin practicing austerities, at the end he shall obtain a hundredfold fruit; of this there is no doubt. || 50 ||
For one who gives the land of Jambudvīpa, who frequents all sacred fords, who performs all forms of austerity, and who makes his dwelling everywhere; || 51 ||
For the giver of all gifts and the lord of all accomplishments, there is indeed rebirth; but for the devotee of the Great Lord, there is none.
The lords of the worlds behold the fall of innumerable Brahmās;
they are reborn on Maṇidvīpa, in the supreme abode of the Śrī Devī.
And those who worship the gods and mantras, having abandoned their human bodies,
attain divine forms and sovereign power that are free from birth, death, and old age.
Having attained a form similar to that of the Goddess and performing service to her,
they behold on the Island of Jewels (Maṇidvīpa) the destruction of the world along with its divisions.
O gods and Siddhas, they vanish, casting off their human bodies along with their divine splendor and forms that ward off birth, death, and old age. (56)
He who offers tulasī to Hari during the month of Kārttika rejoices in the abode of Hari for a duration equal to three yugas.
Having again attained a good birth, he will certainly obtain devotion to Hari;
he shall become the foremost among those who have conquered their senses on the earth of Bhārata. 58.
He who bathes in the middle of the Gaṅgā at the time of dawn rejoices in the abode of Hari for sixty thousand yugas. (19)

Having again attained a noble birth, he will certainly obtain the mantra of Viṣṇu;
and casting off the human body, he goes once more to the abode of Hari.
There is no returning from Vaikuṇṭha to the surface of the earth;
one performs service to Hari and likewise attains the state of having the same form as Him (sārūpya).
He who bathes daily in the Gaṅgā becomes as pure on earth as the sun;
he certainly obtains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice at every step.
The earth is instantly purified by the dust of his very feet,
and he rejoices in Vaikuṇṭha as long as the moon and sun endure.
Furthermore, having attained a good birth, he will certainly obtain devotion to Hari;
liberated while living, exceedingly radiant, he shall become the foremost among ascetics.
Devoted to his own duty, pure, learned, and having conquered his senses—
he is like the sun that burns intensely between the signs of Pisces and Cancer.
He who gives even water well-scented in Bhārata rejoices on Kailāsa for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
Furthermore, having attained a good birth, he shall be handsome and happy;
he shall be a devotee of Śiva and radiant.
As a devotee of Śiva and full of splendor, he shall master the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. || 67 ||
He who gives a gift of barley flour to a twice-born man during the month of Vaiśākha rejoices in the abode of Śiva for as many years as there are grains of dust in that flour.
Indeed, the descendant of Bharata who performs the vow of Kṛṣṇa-janmāṣṭamī is liberated from the sins committed in a hundred lifetimes; there is no doubt about this. (69)
He too rejoices in Vaikuṇṭha for as long as the fourteen Indras endure;
then, having attained a noble birth once more, he will certainly obtain devotion to Kṛṣṇa.
He who observes Śivarātri right here in this land of Bhārata rejoices in the world of Śiva for the duration of seven manvantaras.
He who offers a bilva leaf to Śiva on the night of Śivarātri [attains the same].
There, with a pair of vessels, he rejoices in the abode of Śiva.
Furthermore, having attained a good birth, he will certainly obtain devotion to Śiva;

Or whoever, in the month of Caitra or Māgha, worships Śaṅkara while observing the vow, and dances with devotion day and night holding a cane in hand; ||| 74 ||
Whether for a month, or half a month, or for ten, seven, or even two days,

Indeed, that man who observes Śrī Rāmanavamī in Bhārata rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu for the duration of seven Manvantaras.
Furthermore, having attained a good birth, one will certainly obtain devotion to Rāma;
such a person shall become the foremost among those who have conquered their senses, great, and wealthy. (77)
O virtuous lady, he who performs the great autumnal festival with buffaloes, goats, rams, donkeys, hares, and other such animals; || 78 ||
By means of new garments, offerings of incense and lamps, as well as dances, songs, musical instruments, and various festive auspicious rites,
he too shall dwell in the world of Śiva for the duration of seven manvantaras; thereafter,
having attained a good birth, that man shall possess pure intellect.
He attains incomparable prosperity that increases his sons and grandsons;
endowed with great power, he is accompanied by elephants and horses.
He shall indeed become a sovereign lord of kings, of this there is no doubt;
thereafter, having reached the eighth day of the bright fortnight, he who worships Mahālakṣmī—
Having offered her the sixteen excellent articles of worship with devotion for one fortnight in the sacred field of Bhārata, [he attains the fruit]. || 83 ||
He shall also dwell in Goloka for as long as fourteen Indras reign;
then, having attained a noble birth once more, he shall become the sovereign lord of the kings of kings.
And on the full moon day of Kārttika, having formed the circle of the Rāsa dance, he likewise made a hundred cowherds and a hundred cowherdesses. (85)
In India, one should worship Śrī Kṛṣṇa together with Rādhā with devotion upon a stone slab or in an image, offering the sixteen types of ritual services (upacāras). (86)
He shall dwell in Goloka for as long as the lifespan of Brahmā;
then, returning once more to Bhārata, he will certainly attain devotion to Kṛṣṇa.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 30:
Having gradually attained very firm devotion to Hari, O wonderful one, [one receives] the mantra.
And having cast off the body, he goes once again to Goloka. || 88 ||
Then, becoming the foremost of the attendants (pārṣada), he shall attain the same form as Kṛṣṇa;
there shall be no falling back for him again, and he shall become a remover of old age and death.
Whoever observes either the Śukla (bright) or the Kṛṣṇa (dark) Ekādaśī,
he too rejoices in Vaikuṇṭha for as long as the lifespan of Brahmā endures.
Returning once more to Bhārata, one will certainly attain devotion to Kṛṣṇa;
indeed, in due course, one makes that singular devotion to Hari very firm. (91)
Having cast off the body, he goes once again to Goloka;
then, having attained the same form as Kṛṣṇa, he becomes an attendant (pārṣada).
There is no falling back from that state for him, and he becomes the remover of old age and death. 92.
And on the twelfth day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada, the man who worships Śakra [attains the fruit]. || 93 ||
For sixty thousand years he is honored in the world of Śakra,
[having performed this on] a Sunday, during a solar transit (saṃkrānti), or on the seventh day of the bright fortnight.
He who, having worshipped the Sun, partakes of sacrificial food (haviṣyānna) in Bhārata,
is honored in the world of the Sun for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
Having returned to Bhārata, he shall become healthy and endowed with prosperity;
for whoever worships Sāvitrī on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Jyeṣṭha. (96)
He is honored in the world of Brahmā for the duration of seven manvantaras; then, returning again to the earth, he becomes illustrious and possessed of incomparable valor. 97.
He who worships Sarasvatī on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha shall become long-lived, possessed of knowledge, and endowed with prosperity. (18)
Having offered the sixteen services with self-restraint and devotion, one is honored on Maṇidvīpa day and night for as long as Brahmā exists. 99.
And having attained rebirth once more, he shall become a wise and learned poet;

In Bhārata, he shall remain for as long as life lasts, endowed with devotion;
and in the abode of Viṣṇu, he shall stay for twice the number of years equal to the hairs on a cow's body.
He rejoices together with Hari through the auspicious delights of play;
at the conclusion of that, having returned once more, he shall become the sovereign lord of the kings of kings.
In Bhārata, he who feeds sweet food to the Brāhmaṇas becomes illustrious, possessed of sons, learned, endowed with knowledge, and happy in every respect. (103)
He rejoices in the abode of Viṣṇu for as many years as there are hairs on his body;

O Bhārata, he who speaks or indeed gives the names of Hari becomes wise, long-lived, illustrious, and possessed of incomparable valor. (105)
For the duration of a Yuga, he is honored in the world of Viṣṇu;

If the fruit [of merit] in the field of Nārāyaṇa were to be ten millionfold, it belongs to him who indeed recites ten million names of Hari in the field of Nārāyaṇa. 107.
Freed from all sins, he shall certainly become liberated while living;
he shall not undergo rebirth, for he is glorified in Vaikuṇṭha.
He shall attain the state of having the same form as Viṣṇu, and for him there shall be no falling back;
even that devotee of Viṣṇu shall obtain and reach the state of being identical in form with Viṣṇu.
He who constantly worships Śiva after fashioning an earthen liṅga reaches the abode of Śiva for as long as he lives. || 110 ||
One is glorified in the world of Śiva for as many years as there are particles of dust in the clod of earth;

One who constantly worships the stone and drinks the water from the stone is honored in Vaikuṇṭha for as long as a hundred Brahmās exist.
Then, having obtained a rebirth as a rare devotee of Hari, he is glorified in the world of Viṣṇu; for him there shall be no falling away.

In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter thirty-four.
He who, having bathed in all the sacred fords and having circumambulated the earth, attains liberation; he shall not be born again on this earth.

shall occupy the throne of Śakra for as many years as there are hairs on the horse's body.
A human being obtains four times the fruit of the Rājasūya sacrifice;

O fair-faced one, it was performed in the past by Viṣṇu and by Brahmā,
and by Śaṅkara, the Great Lord, during the destruction of the Asura Tripura.
O beautiful one, the Śakti-sacrifice is the foremost among all sacrifices;

O Satī, in former times, Dakṣa prepared a great sacrifice accompanied by vast provisions,
wherein a quarrel arose between Dakṣa and Śaṅkara.

for that reason, the moon-crested Lord destroyed Dakṣa’s sacrifice.
In ancient times, that Dakṣa, the lord of progeny, performed a sacrifice for the goddess;
as did Dharma, Śeṣa, and Kardama.
Svāyambhuva Manu, his son Priyavrata, Śiva, Sanatkumāra, Kapila, and Dhruva; || 124 ||
One certainly attains the fruit of thousands of Rājasūya sacrifices.

Furthermore, one who lives for a hundred years shall certainly become liberated while living (jīvanmukta).
By means of knowledge and splendor, one shall indeed become equal to Viṣṇu in this world. || 126 ||
Just as Viṣṇu is among the gods, and Nārada among the Vaiṣṇavas;

In the Purāṇas, the Vedas, and the Itihāsas everywhere, the lotus-feet of the Lord have been described as the very essence. (136)
Describing that [deity], meditating upon that, chanting the names and qualities of that, as well as praising, remembering, saluting, and reciting [the mantra] of that. (137)
O virtuous lady, the constant consumption of the water from his feet and the food offerings is approved by all;
indeed, this is desired by everyone.
Worship eternally the Supreme Brahman, who is beyond all qualities and the supreme nature;
accept him as your husband, my child, and dwell happily in the palace.
This auspicious ripening of karma for human beings has been told to you;
it is desired by all, approved by all, and is the supreme bestower of the knowledge of reality. 140.
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 30 ||
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter thirty-one.
Now begins the thirty-first chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having heard the glorification of Śakti from the mouth of Yama, Sāvitrī,
her eyes filled with tears and her hair standing on end with joy, spoke again to Yama.
Sāvitrī said:
"The glorification of Śakti is dharma, the cause of the upliftment of all;
it removes birth, death, and old age for both the listeners and the speakers. (2)
The highest state for the Dānavas and the Siddhas is through austerity;
for those of yoga and the Vedas, it is the glorification and service of the All-pervading Lord.
Liberation, immortality, and even the attainment of all supernatural powers do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit belonging to one who serves Śrī Śakti. ||4||
"O best among the knowers of the Vedas, tell me by what method I may worship; for I have heard the captivating account of the ripening of the auspicious deeds of men. (5)
"And you ought to explain to me that impure ripening of karma.
Having spoken thus, O Brahmin, Satī, with her neck bowed low in devotion, [continued].
And she praised the King of Dharma with a hymn spoken in the Vedas.
Sāvitrī said:
"In ancient times, at Puṣkara, the Sun-god propitiated Dharma through austerity."
I bow to Dharmarāja, the son whom Dharma-sūrya obtained, who is equal toward all beings and the witness of everything. 8.
Therefore, I bow down to that which is called the pacification of names, by which the ultimate end has been made for all living beings in the universe. (9)
I bow to that Kṛtānta (the Ender), who acts in accordance with desires at the proper time;
he wields the staff for the sake of punishing and purifying the wicked.
I bow to that wielder of the staff, who is the teacher of all living beings and who indeed pervades the entire universe, remaining eternally present within all.
I bow down to that Time which is exceedingly difficult to ward off;
he who is an ascetic, established in Brahman, self-restrained, and has conquered his senses.
I bow to that Yama, who bestows the fruits of karma upon living beings;
he is one who delights in his own self, is all-knowing, and is a friend to those who perform meritorious deeds. 13.
I bow to that meritorious friend who brings affliction to sinners;
he whose birth was from a portion of Brahmā, blazing with the splendor of Brahman.
"I bow down to that Lord who meditates upon the Supreme Brahman";
having spoken thus, O Sage, Sāvitrī prostrated herself before Yama.
Yama spoke to Śaktibhajan regarding the ripening of karma:
"Whoever, having risen in the morning, should recite this *Yamāṣṭaka* daily," (16)
From whom he has no fear, and he is liberated from all evil—
if even a great sinner should recite this daily, endowed with devotion.
Yama makes him completely pure through a definitive array of bodies. || 17 ||
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. ||31||
Now begins the thirty-second chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having bestowed the great mantra of the seed-syllable Māyā according to the prescribed rites, [he spoke].
And the son of the Sun spoke to her concerning the impure ripening of her karma.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter thirty-two.
The King of Dharma said:
"A human being does not go to hell as a result of the ripening of auspicious karma;
however, I shall describe the ripening of inauspicious karma—listen attentively. (2)
O beautiful lady, according to the various distinctions of the Purāṇas and the differences in names,
the individual soul goes to various kinds of heavens by means of its own karmas.
Through the ripening of auspicious karma, a person goes to hell by means of their actions;
and through evil deeds, a person likewise goes to various kinds of hells. (4)
And there are various kinds of pits for the hells, according to the measurements of diverse scriptures and according to the distinctions of karma. (5)
O child, these doctrines are extensive, they bring affliction to those who suffer,
they are terrifying, dreadful, and contemptible.
There are eighty-six sacrificial pits (kuṇḍas), and there are others as well;
learn their names as they are well-known in the Śruti.
The fire-pit, the boiling-pit, the terrifying alkaline-pit, the excrement-pit, the urine-pit, and the unbearable phlegm-pit. ||8||
The pit of feces, the pit of pus, and likewise the pit of fat;
the pit of semen, the pit of blood, and the loathsome pit of tears.
The pit of bodily filth, the pit of the ears and other [orifices], the pit of marrow, the pit of flesh, and the impassable pit of crocodiles. (10)
The pit of body hair, the pit of hair, and the pit of bones are difficult to cross;
the copper pit and the iron pit are intensely heated and grant great suffering. || 11 ||

The pit of leather (carmakuṇḍa) and the pit of boiling liquor (taptasurākuṇḍa) are proclaimed; as well as the pit of sharp-edged blades (tīkṣṇakaṭakakuṇḍa), the pit of poison-water (viṣoda), and the pit of venom (vipakuṇḍaka). ||12||
The heated pit of oil, the unbearable pit of spears,
the pit of worms, the pit of excrement, and the terrible pit of serpents.
They give birth to the pit of mosquitoes, the pit of gadflies, the terrible pit of venomous serpents,
and the pits of those with diamond-like fangs and of scorpions.
The pit of arrows, the pit of spears, and the terrifying pit of swords;
the pit of cows, the pit of crocodiles, and the pit of crows—a dwelling place of sorrow. (15)
The churning pit, the seed pit, the unbearable diamond pit, the pit of heated stones, and the pit of sharp stones. ||16||
The Lālā-kuṇḍa, the Masī-kuṇḍa, and likewise the Cūrṇa-kuṇḍa;
the Cakra-kuṇḍa, the Vakrakuṇḍa, and the exceedingly formidable Kūrmakuṇḍa. || 17 ||
O lady of pure smiles, there are the pits of flames, the pit of ashes, and the pit of burning embers;
the heated needle, the sword-leaf, the razor’s edge, and the needle-mouth.
Gokāmukha, Nakramukha, Gajadaṃśa, and Gomukha; Kumbhīpāka, Kālasūtra, Matsyoda, and Kṛmitantuka. (19)
The Pāṃsubhojya, the Pāśaveṣṭa, the Śūlaprota, the Prakampana,
the Ulkāmukha, the Andhakūpa, the Vedhana, and likewise the Tāḍana.
The lattice-hole, the powdering of the body, the crushing, the drying, the winnowing-basket, the flame-mouthed, the smoke-blindness, and the serpent-encirclement. (21)
O Sāvitrī, these are the pits that inflict suffering upon sinners,
and they are constantly guarded by millions of hosts of Kiṅkaras.
With staffs in hand, nooses in hand, intoxicated with pride, and terrifying; with spears in hand, maces in hand, and swords in hand, they were exceedingly dreadful.
They were joined with darkness, devoid of compassion, and irresistible from all sides; they were radiant, fearless, and had eyes that were coppery-red and tawny.
O Lord, he was seen by those devoted to yoga who possessed supernatural powers and assumed various forms, as well as by sinners whose death was imminent and by all those who lived by sinful means.
It was filled with all those devoted to their own duties— devotees of Śakti, Sūrya, and Gaṇeśa—
as well as invisible merit-makers, Siddhas, and Yogins.
Whether they are devoted to their own duties, widely renowned, independent, powerful, fearless, or Vaiṣṇavas seen in dreams— [by such persons it should be performed].
O virtuous lady, this description of the number of sacrificial pits has been told to you.
"Learn from me as I tell you in which pool they have their dwelling.
Thus ends the thirty-second chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa. || 32 ||
