whose very nature is splendor in the moon, and who is adorned by the solar disc.
In ornaments, jewels, fruits, and waters;
in kings, queens, celestial women, and in houses. || 21 ||
In all grains, in garments, in consecrated places, in images of the gods, in auspicious objects, and in balance-scales; ||22||
She was enchanting amidst rubies and pearls, amidst garlands,
amidst the finest gems and tawny elephants, and amidst milk and sandalwood.
On the beautiful branches of the *vṛna* tree and among objects of fresh clouds,
that Goddess was worshipped by Nārāyaṇa in Vaikuṇṭha.
O Sage, she was worshipped with devotion by Brahmā in the second [kalpa], by Śaṅkara in the third, and by Viṣṇu in the Kṣīroda ocean in Bhārata.
By Svāyambhuva Manu, by the lords of men everywhere, by the lords of sages, by the lords of munis, and by virtuous householders, [this was established] in this world. (26)
She is worshipped by the Gandharvas, Nāgas, and others in the netherworlds (pātālas);
and on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Bhādrapada, worship was performed for her by Brahmā.
And with devotion until the end of the fortnight, O Nārada, on the auspicious Tuesday in the months of Caitra, Pauṣa, and Bhādra. || 28 ||
And she was worshipped with devotion by Viṣṇu throughout the three worlds;
at the end of the year, on the auspicious day of the sun's entry into Capricorn (Makara-saṃkrānti) during the month of Pauṣa, she was invoked in the midst [of the assembly].
Manu worshipped her; she became the one who exists throughout the three worlds.
Worshipped by Mahendra, she is Maṅgalā, the auspicious one who is auspiciousness itself.
In the Śrīmad Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 40:
Together with Kedāra, Nīla, Subala, and Nala.
By Dhruva, Uttānapāda, Śakra, and likewise by Bali.
And by Kaśyapa, Dakṣa, Kardama, Vivasvat, Priyavrata, Candra, Kuvera, and indeed by Vāyu. ||32||
Honored by Yama, by Vahni, and indeed by Varuṇa,
she is thus everywhere honored and always saluted by all.
She is the presiding goddess of all sovereignty, whose very nature is every form of prosperity.
Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 39 ||
Now begins the fortieth chapter.
Nārada said:
She is the beloved of Nārāyaṇa, the excellent one who dwells in Vaikuṇṭha.
The eternal Mahālakṣmī is the presiding goddess of Vaikuṇṭha.
How did that goddess, the daughter of the ocean, come to be on earth?
By whom was she praised in the beginning? You should explain that to me. (2)
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Nārada, in ancient times, due to the curse of Durvāsas, Indra was deprived of his fortune, as were the hosts of gods, and they came to dwell in the world of mortals.
O Nārada, Lakṣmī, having abandoned heaven and other realms, became enraged and deeply distressed; she went and merged into Mahālakṣmī in Vaikuṇṭha.
Then, all of them, distressed by grief and other emotions, went to the assembly hall of Brahmā;
and placing Brahmā at their head, they proceeded to Vaikuṇṭha itself.
In Vaikuṇṭha, the gods took refuge in the supreme Nārāyaṇa;
they were filled with extreme wretchedness, their throats, lips, and palates parched.
Then, by the command of the Ancient Puruṣa,
Lakṣmī herself became the Daughter of the Ocean through a portion of her being, the embodiment of all prosperity.
Having thus churned the Ocean of Milk together with the hosts of Daityas,
the gods obtained Mahālakṣmī, and Viṣṇu beheld her.
Having granted boons to Surā and the others, and having given a forest garland to Viṣṇu, she,
with a gracious countenance and well-pleased, gave them to the one who reclines upon the Ocean of Milk.
O Nārada, the gods also regained their kingdom, which had been seized by the asuras.
Having worshipped her together as a group, they became free from all calamities everywhere.
Nārada said:
O Brahmin, how did Durvāsas, the best of sages and a knower of the truth of Brahman, once utter a curse? By what fault, O Brahmin, was he provoked in the past? 11.
In what form did the gods and others churn the ocean, and by what hymn of praise did that Goddess manifest herself in person? (12)
"Or who among those two became victorious? Tell me that, O Lord.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
"In ancient times, the sovereign of the three worlds was intoxicated by the drinking of honey-wine."
The lustful one sported in secret with Rambhā;
having engaged in play with that amorous woman, his mind was captivated by her.
His mind agitated by desire, he remained there in that great forest,
watching the best of sages as he departed from Vaikuṇṭha for the peak of Kailāsa.
Indra beheld Durvāsas, blazing with Brahmanic luster,
the Lord who possessed the brilliance of a thousand suns at midday in the summer season.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter forty: [He] had the appearance of molten gold and was intensely radiant with a mass of matted locks.
A white sacred thread, a staff like that of a thief, and a water-pot. || 17 ||
He bore a most brilliant sectarian mark (tilaka) resembling the moon, and was accompanied by hundreds of thousands of disciples who had mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas. ||18||
Seeing him, Purandara, though distracted, bowed his head;
then, filled with joy, he praised the group of disciples with devotion.
The Sage, together with his disciples, bestowed auspicious blessings upon him, as well as the beautiful Pārijāta flower given by Viṣṇu. (20)
That flower destroys old age, disease, and death; it removes sorrow and brings about liberation.
Yet Śakra, intoxicated by the prosperity of his kingdom, took that flower.
At that very moment, he placed a flower upon the head of the elephant;
by the mere touch of it, the elephant was transformed in both appearance and quality.
Suddenly, by virtue of his splendor and youth, he became equal to Viṣṇu;
and the lordly elephant, abandoning Śakra, departed for the terrible forest.
O sage, Mahendra was unable to protect it by his own splendor;
and seeing Śakra having abandoned that flower, the lord of sages [spoke].
Greatly enraged and filled with fury, he spoke to him and uttered a curse.
The sage said:
"O you, intoxicated by prosperity, how can you insult me? (25)
A flower given by me, or an offering of food, fruit, or water presented with pride upon the head of an elephant, is indeed offered to Viṣṇu. (26)
One should enjoy [the fruit] merely by its attainment; through renunciation, one becomes Brahman.
But he whose prosperity has fallen away and whose intellect is ruined shall become a ruined city.
He who would abandon the auspicious *naivedya* of Viṣṇu that has come to him by fortune, and he who eats what was offered to Viṣṇu merely because it has been obtained—he is not a devotee. (28)
Having delivered a hundred men, he himself becomes liberated while living, he who daily offers food as an oblation and bows down to Hari. (29)
Whoever worships him with devotion becomes equal to Viṣṇu;
by the mere touch of his breath, a sacred bathing place (tīrtha) is immediately purified. ||30||
The earth is purified [of the taints of] the food of an unchaste woman, the food of one whose husband is not a hero, and likewise the food of a Śūdra’s funeral feast (śrāddha).
O fool, by the dust of his feet, you have immediately incurred the sin of eating meat that was not offered to Hari,
as well as the sin of offering a Śiva-liṅga which was given by one who performs sacrifices for Śūdras.
The food of physicians and twice-born men, likewise the food of temple-priests (devala), the food of those who purchase girls and the like, the food of those who live off their wives,
food that is leavings, stale food, and what remains after all have eaten— [these are forbidden].
And likewise, the food of twice-born men who have sexual intercourse with women who should not be approached. ||34||
And the food of twice-born men who have not been initiated, of those who carry out the dead, and likewise the food of twice-born men who approach women who should not be approached; (35)

The food of those who betray friends, the food of the ungrateful, the food of those who violate trust, the food of those who give false testimony, and likewise the food of Brahmins [who accept such gifts]; 36.
All these are purified by eating the food offered to Viṣṇu;
even a dog-eater who serves Viṣṇu may uplift ten million generations of his lineage. (37)
A person who is not a devotee of Hari is incapable of protecting even himself;
yet, out of ignorance, he might even consume the food offering (naivedya) of Viṣṇu. (38)
One is liberated from the sins accumulated over seven births; there is no doubt about this.
Having understood this, one who accepts it with devotion knows that which is indeed unknowable even to Viṣṇu.
O Hari, one is certainly liberated from the sins accumulated over ten million births because a flower was placed with pride upon the head of the elephant. (40)
Therefore, let Lakṣmī abandon you and go to the abode of Hari;
I am a devotee of Nārāyaṇa and I fear neither the gods nor Brahmā.
What others can I reckon against Time, Death, and Old Age? And what will your father, Kaśyapa the Lord of Creatures, do for you? (42)
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 40.
O Hari, for me who am free from doubt, both Nṛhaspati and Guru are my teachers;
yet, the supreme worship belongs to him upon whose head this flower is placed.
Having heard this, Mahendra grasped the foot of the sage and wept aloud, afflicted by grief and overwhelmed with fear; he spoke to him thus: || 44 ||
Mahendra said:
"O Lord, O dispeller of illusion, a fitting curse has been bestowed upon me;
I do not ask for my lost prosperity back, but grant me some measure of knowledge. (45)
Sovereignty is the seed of calamities, the cause of the concealment of knowledge, an axe for the path to liberation, and an obstacle to the Lord. (46)
The sage said:
One who is blinded by the darkness of worldly prosperity does not perceive the supreme path to liberation, which is the seed-sprout for overcoming birth, death, old age, sorrow, and disease. (47)
He was intoxicated with pride and utterly deluded, just like one intoxicated by liquor;
even though he was surrounded by kinsmen, O Hari, they regarded him as nothing more than a kinsman.
Intoxicated by the pride of prosperity, blinded by sense objects, and overwhelmed,
the passionate person of rajasic nature does not perceive the path of sattva.
The blind regarding objects is said to be of two kinds: that characterized by passion (rājasa) and that characterized by darkness (tāmasa).
One who is ignorant of the scriptures is tāmasa, while one who knows the scriptures is remembered as rājasa. || 50 ||
And the scripture, O bull among gods, reveals two kinds of paths:
one is the seed of worldly involvement, and the other is the cause of liberation.
At the beginning of worldly activity, living beings move along the path of suffering, acting according to their own will, with cheerfulness, and continuously without opposition. 52.
Driven by greed for honey and honored with ease through hardship,
he arrives at the seed-portion which, in its final transformation, brings about birth, death, and old age.
Having wandered joyfully through many successive births, one proceeds in due order through various wombs ordained by one's own karma. (54)
Then, through the grace of Īśvara, he attains the company of the virtuous;
for among hundreds and thousands, only one becomes a means of crossing the ocean of worldly existence.
The saintly one should show the path to liberation by means of the lamp of reality;
then the living being exerts effort toward the shattering of bondage.
Through the connection of many births, by means of austerity and fasting,
one shall then attain the supreme path to liberation, which is free from obstacles and bestows happiness.
"O Purandara, that which you ask has been heard from the mouth of my guru;
having heard those words of the sage, he became free from passion. (58)
O Brahmin, his dispassion increased day by day;
having gone from the sage's abode to his own home, he beheld the Blessed Goddess.
It was crowded with Daityas and hosts of Asuras, filled with fear,
beset by calamities, and in some places bereft of sons and kinsmen.
Seeing her deprived of father, mother, wife, and others, exceedingly fickle, and seized by enemies, he went toward Vākpati.
On the bank of the Mandākinī, Śakra beheld his guru, the Lord,
standing in the waters of the Gaṅgā, meditating upon the supreme Brahman.
Facing the sun and facing the east, with faces turned in every direction,
his eyes filled with tears, his body bristling with joy, and endowed with supreme bliss.
Most excellent and most venerable, most righteous and served by the best, most beloved among circles of kinsmen and most preeminent among the wise. (64)
Seeing his elder brother, the enemy of the gods, whom the hosts of brothers disliked, muttering prayers there, the Lord of the Gods stood still.
At the end of the watch, seeing his preceptor, he rose and prostrated;
having bowed at the lotus-feet of his teacher, he wept aloud again and again.
The Lord of the Gods related the account, including the curse of Brahmā and so forth,
as well as the subsequent attainment of boons and the acquisition of most rare knowledge,
and how his own city was seized by his enemies in due course. (67)
Having heard the words of the disciple, Subuddhi, the best among speakers, [replied].
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter forty.
Bṛhaspati, his eyes bloodshot with anger, spoke as follows:
The Guru said:
"O best of gods, everything has been heard; do not weep, listen to my words. (69)
For a man of wisdom is never cowardly in the face of adversity;
for both prosperity and adversity are transitory and take the form of toil.
It occurs for both of them as well, and indeed for all beings, constantly in birth after birth.
Moreover, one's own lamentation is dependent on past karma;
for it has been said throughout all of Bhārata that the fruit of one's own performed actions must be experienced. (72)
By the very sequence of the wheel's rim, a person experiences whatever is auspicious or inauspicious as the fruit of his own karma;

for karma that has not been experienced does not perish even in hundreds of millions of eons. In this regard, whatever karma—whether auspicious or inauspicious—has been committed must necessarily be experienced.
Thus it has been stated in the Veda and by Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Self.
Having addressed the Lotus-born One within the branch of the Sāmaveda,
[he spoke] regarding the remainder of the experiences of birth for all those who have performed their actions.
For indeed, in accordance with their own actions, they receive the curse of a Brahmin or a blessing of auspiciousness through their deeds, both in Bhārata and elsewhere. (76)
Through action one may attain great fortune, and through action one may also attain poverty; the karma accumulated over ten million lifetimes follows living beings.
For indeed, O Purandara, one cannot abandon the fruit of actions without experiencing it, just as one cannot escape the shadow;
this holds true across differences of time, place, and recipient. (78)
Indeed, there may even be a state of deficiency or excess due to one's actions;
yet, through the gift of actual objects, the merit remains equal day after day. (79)
O God, on different days the merit is ten-millionfold, or incalculable, or even greater than that; and when objects are given in a level place, the merit is equal [to the value of the gift]. 80.
Depending on the difference in location, the merit may be ten millionfold or even greater than that;
however, when the recipient is equal, the merit for the objects [given] belongs equally to both the donor and the maker.
When the recipient is distinguished, the fruit is a hundredfold, or incalculable, or even greater than that;
just as crops may yield less or more than expected.
O Brahmin, just as there is a difference in yield for farmers depending on the type of field or the quality of the vessel,
so too does a gift given on an ordinary day bear equal fruit [in all cases].
On the new moon day coinciding with the sun's transit (saṃkrānti), the fruit shall be a hundredfold;
and on the full moon day of the Cāturmāsya period, the fruit is indeed infinite.
The fruit at the time of a lunar eclipse is said to be ten millionfold, and at a solar eclipse, it shall be ten times even greater than that. ||85||
That which is called an inexhaustible, incalculable fruit in the Akṣaya [Tithi], likewise there would be a preponderance of fruit on other auspicious days (puṇyāha). || 86 ||
In bathing, in recitation, and in other meritorious acts—in this way, the fruit of men's actions is to be understood everywhere. (87)
Just as in the case of giving, so too does the potter creator fashion a jar from clay upon the earth by means of a staff, a wheel, a bowl-shaped mold, and a spinning motion.
In the same way, the Creator bestows the fruit according to the thread of karma;
worship that Nārāyaṇa by whose command this universe was created. (89)
He is the ordainer of the ordainer and the protector of the protector in the three worlds;
he is the creator of the creator and the destroyer of the destroyer—the death of Death itself.
"Śaṅkara has said that for one who remembers Madhusūdana even during a great calamity in saṃsāra, prosperity shall arise from that very misfortune. (91)
Having spoken thus, O Nārada, the knower of reality embraced the Lord of the Gods, gave him auspicious blessings, and awakened him to his desired goal.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 40 ||
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter 4.1.
Now begins the forty-first chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Brahmā, having meditated upon Hari, Hari went to the assembly hall of Brahmā.
Placing Bṛhaspati at their head, together with all the hosts of gods.
Having gone quickly to the world of Brahmā and beheld the Lotus-born One,
all the deities, together with Indra and their preceptor, prostrated themselves.
The preceptor of the gods related the account to Brahmā;
having heard that, the lotus-seated one laughed and spoke to Mahendra.
Brahmā said:
"O child, you are born of my lineage; you are my wise great-grandson.
You are the disciple of Bṛhaspati and yourself the sovereign of the gods."
And your maternal grandfather Dakṣa was a devotee of Viṣṇu and possessed great prowess;
how could he, whose three lineages were pure, have been filled with ego? (5)
How could he who has a mother devoted to her husband, a father who is pure and self-controlled, and a maternal grandfather and uncle [of the same character], ever become possessed of egoism? (3)
Due to the fault of his father, the fault of his maternal grandfather,
and the fault of his preceptor— by these three faults, a person will certainly become a sinner against Hari.
The Blessed One is the inner self of all, dwelling within all bodies;
when He departs from one's body, that corpse becomes like wood in an instant.
I am the mind and the lord of the senses; for Śaṅkara is the very form of knowledge.
Viṣṇu is the vital breath, and the goddess Satī is Prakṛti and the intellect.
Sleep and the other powers—all these are the modalities (kalās) of Prakṛti;
and the individual soul (jīva), who bears a body for experience, is the reflection of the Self. 10.
When the Lord of the self departs from the body, all [the senses] go forth in agitation, just as followers accompany a king of men traveling upon his path. || 11 ||
I, Śiva, Śeṣa, Viṣṇu, Dharma, and Mahāvirāṭ—we and you are all his portions and his devotees; yet that very flower has been insulted by you.
That lotus flower with which Śiva’s foot was worshipped was given there by Durvāsas; it was cast down by you through fate—
that very flower which had fallen from the lotus-foot of Kṛṣṇa and rested upon his head.
And the worship of that [deity] should take place before all the gods.
Indeed, you have been deceived by fate; for fate is more powerful.
Who indeed is able to protect a foolish person who is devoid of fortune? || 14-15 ||
That Goddess Śrī has now departed in anger because of your rejection of the *nirmālya* offered by Kṛṣṇa;
therefore, go now to Vaikuṇṭha along with me and your preceptor.
"By worshipping Śrīnātha there, you shall obtain prosperity after a great time.
Having spoken thus, Brahmā, together with all the hosts of gods, [departed]. (17)
Having gone there, he beheld the Blessed One, the eternal Supreme Brahman, whose nature is splendor and who was blazing with his own radiance.
He possesses a splendor equal to hundreds of millions of suns at midday in summer;
he is peaceful, without beginning, middle, or end, the beloved of Lakṣmī, and infinite.
The Lord was joined by Sarasvatī with her four arms and four feet, and was surrounded by the four Vedas with devotion and by the Gaṅgā. ||20||
Led by Brahmā, all the gods bowed their heads to him;
humble with devotion and with eyes full of tears, they praised the Supreme Lord.
Brahmā himself, with palms joined in reverence, related the account;
all the deities wept, having been deprived of their respective offices. 22.
He beheld the host of gods seized by calamity, overwhelmed with fear,
stripped of their jewel-ornaments, and deprived of their mounts and other possessions.

Seeing him devoid of splendor, robbed of his glory, lusterless, utterly terrified, and overcome with fear, the Destroyer of the Fear of Saṃsāra spoke: śobhāśūnyaṃ hataśrīkaṃ niṣprabhaṃ sabhayaṃ param | uvāca kātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhavabhītivibhañjanaḥ || 24 ||
In the glorious Śrīmad Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter four. The Blessed Lord said:
"Do not fear, O Brahmin, nor you gods; what cause for fear is there while I stand here?
I shall grant you unfailing prosperity that increases supreme sovereignty. (25)
Furthermore, please listen to some words of mine that are appropriate for the occasion—words that are beneficial, true, essential, and conducive to future happiness. (26)
Just as the countless people dwelling in the universe are perpetually under my control,
so too am I dependent on my devotees and lack independence.
Whomever my devotee, who is intent on me and unrestrained, becomes angry with, in that person's house I certainly do not dwell, even together with Padmā. 28.
Durvāsas is a portion of Śaṅkara, a Vaiṣṇava, and one devoted to me;
it was because of his curse that I, along with Lakṣmī, came from your house.
Where there is no sound of the conch, no *tulasī*, no worship of Śiva, and no feeding of Brahmins, there Lakṣmī does not dwell. (30)
O Brahmin, wherever there is censure of my devotees or of me among the gods,
Mahālakṣmī becomes greatly enraged and consequently suffers defeat.
If that fool who is devoid of devotion to me eats on the day of Hari or even on my birthday,
prosperity departs from his house as well.
He who sells his own daughter for money,
and from whose house a guest does not eat— my beloved departs from that home.
That brahmin who is the son of an unchaste woman, that husband who is a great sinner, and he who goes to the house of a sinner or eats the food of a śrāddha offered by a śūdra; ||34||
Then, greatly enraged, Lakṣmī departed from her abode;
that lowest of the twice-born was devoid of fortune and had cremated the corpses of Śūdras. || 35 ||
The goddess who dwells in the lotus departs from the house of that man in anger—of him who is a cook for Śūdras or a Brāhmaṇa who drives oxen. || 36 ||
And Kamalā, fearing the drinking of his water, departs from that man's house;
for he is a twice-born who is impure of heart, cruel, violent, and a reviler. ||37||
The Brahmin who officiates for a Śūdra and the Goddess depart from that house; likewise, the Mother of the World departs from him who eats the food of a woman without a husband. 38.
Where one cuts grass with fingernails or scratches the earth with them, and where a Brahmin goes away from that house disappointed—that is what is dear to me. 39.
The twice-born who eats at sunrise, the Brāhmaṇa who sleeps during the day, and he who engages in sexual intercourse by day—he departs from me as one I do not love. 40.
That brahmin who is devoid of proper conduct, he who accepts gifts from a śūdra,
and that fool who is uninitiated— verily, my beloved departs from him.
Indeed, that virtuous woman departs from the house of one who has oily feet, who sleeps naked, who is weak in knowledge, and who speaks incessantly with a garrulous tongue. 42.
If one who has bathed his head with oil should touch another part of the body, or play a musical instrument upon his own body, she departs from that house in anger. 43.
That twice-born man who is devoid of vows and fasts, who neglects the twilight prayers, who is impure, and who lacks devotion to Viṣṇu—depart from him, O my beloved. 44.
Indeed, he who reviles a Brāhmaṇa, as well as he who constantly hates him, being a killer of living beings and devoid of compassion, goes [to hell] from every birth. (45)
Wherever there is an image of Hari and likewise the chanting of Hari’s praises, there that Goddess, the most auspicious of all auspicious things, resides. 46.
O Grandfather, wherever there is praise of Kṛṣṇa or his devotee,
and wherever that goddess who is dear to Kṛṣṇa resides constantly;
wherever there is the sound of a conch, a conch-shell, a sacred stone, or a leaf of tulasī—
Service to him, salutation, and meditation—therein she is firmly established. || 48 ||
Where there is worship of the Śiva-liṅga, its glorious praise is auspicious;
there is the worship of Durgā, her qualities, and Padmanivāsinī resides there.
Where there is service to the Brahmins and their auspicious feeding, and where there is the worship of all the gods—there, O lotus-faced one, is the virtuous woman. 50.
Having spoken thus to all the gods, that Lord of Ramā said to me:
"Take birth in the Ocean of Milk by means of a portion [of yourself]. (51)
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter forty-two.
Having spoken thus to her, the Lord of the World spoke again to Brahmā:
"O Lotus-born One, having churned the ocean, give Lakṣmī to the gods."
Having spoken thus, O sage, the beloved of Kamalā entered the inner apartments;
and after some time, the gods went to the Ocean of Milk.
Having made Mount Mandara the churning stick and the tortoise the vessel,
and having made Śeṣa the churning rope, the gods and the asuras churned [the ocean].
They obtained Dhanvantari, the desired nectar, the horse Uccaiḥśravas, various jewels, the jewel among elephants, Lakṣmī, and the Sudarśana discus.
O sage, that virtuous Vaiṣṇavī gave a forest garland to Viṣṇu, the Lord of All, the beautiful one who reclines upon the Ocean of Milk.
Praised and honored by the gods, as well as by Brahmā and Śaṅkara,
she bestowed her vision upon the abode of the gods through liberation from the Brahmin’s curse.
O Nārada, by the grace of Mahālakṣmī and through her granting of boons, the gods regained their own realm, which had been seized by the Daityas and was filled with terror. 58.
Thus has this entire, supreme narrative of Lakṣmī been told—granting happiness and consisting of the essential truth. What more do you wish to hear?
Thus ends the forty-first chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa.
Now begins the forty-second chapter.
Nārada said:
O Lord, the chanting of Hari’s names is auspicious, and that knowledge has been heard by me as supreme;
now please tell me the desired narrative of Lakṣmī, along with its meditation and hymn of praise.
Nārada said: Having previously bathed in the sacred ford and put on two clean garments, Śakra placed a water-pot in the Ocean of Milk and worshipped the six deities.
Then, having worshipped Gaṇeśa, the Sun, Agni, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and Śivā with devotion using flowers, perfumes, and other offerings; || 3 ||
Having invoked Mahālakṣmī, who is the embodiment of supreme sovereignty,
the Goddess of Devas performed her worship with Brahmā as the presiding priest,
while the sages, the Brāhmaṇas, the Guru, and Hari stood before them.
O Sage, [this occurs] among the gods and others, in a holy place, and within Śiva, who is the bliss of knowledge.
Having taken a flower from the pārijāta tree and sprinkled it with sandalwood paste,
O Nārada, he meditated upon the goddess Mahālakṣmī and worshipped her.
Understand that meditation which was formerly given to Brahmā by Hari as declared in the Sāmaveda; through that meditation, I shall speak to you—listen to it. (7)
The Supreme Goddess resides within the pericarp of a thousand-petaled lotus;
she is the Supreme One, whose hands grasp the light of ten million full moons of the autumnal season.
Blazing with her own splendor, pleasant to behold and captivating,
she possessed the luster of molten gold— Satī herself in embodied form.
Richly adorned with jewel ornaments and beautified by yellow garments,
her face bright with a gentle smile, she is eternally established in the prime of youth.
I worship the auspicious Mahālakṣmī, the bestower of all prosperity;
having meditated upon her, who is endowed with manifold virtues, through this meditation. 11.
Having worshipped according to the words of Brahmā, he offered the sixteen types of ritual services with devotion and according to the prescribed rule, each preceded by its respective mantra.
They were praiseworthy, excellent, choice, and diverse;
they were fashioned by Viśvakarman from the essence of priceless jewels.
O Mahālakṣmī, please accept this variegated seat;
here is pure water from the Gaṅgā, which is desired and honored by all. (14)
"O Abode of Kamala, let the water of the Jahnavi, joined with flowers, sandalwood, dūrvā grass, and other offerings, be accepted as the form of the fire that consumes the fuel of sin. (15)
O Lotus-Dweller, please accept this celestial conch containing the embryo of Śaṅkha. *Śrīmad-Devībhāgavatamahāpurāṇa*, Ninth Skandha, Chapter 42.
And fragrant flower oil, as well as fragrant āmalakī fruit. ||16||
O beloved of Śrī Hari, let the seed of bodily beauty be accepted;
O Goddess, let clothing made of cotton and silk be accepted;
and let ornaments made of gems and gold, which increase the adornment of the body, be accepted.
"O Goddess, please accept this jewel, which brings prosperity and serves as an ornament for the sake of beauty. (18)
It is the seed of all beauty, an immediate and supreme producer of splendor, consisting of the resin of trees and combined with fragrant substances and the like. (19)
O beloved of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, please accept this incense and this sacred thread;
O Goddess, please accept this sandalwood paste, fragrant and bestowing happiness. (20)
O Sovereign of the Gods, please accept this lamp, which is the very form of the eye of the world, pure, dispeller of darkness, and the embodiment of bliss. 21.
May you accept this food offering, which takes the form of various oblations, is endowed with diverse flavors, and is exceedingly delicious.
Food is the very nature of Brahman and the cause of the preservation of life; it bestows contentment and nourishment. O Goddess, please accept this food. (23)
O Mahālakṣmī, please accept this well-cooked rice made from śāli grains, mixed with sugar and cow’s milk products, and endowed with delicious flavor—this supreme *paramānna*. (24)
And it was cooked with sugar and cow's milk, delicious and most enchanting. ||25||
Various kinds of delightful cooked foods and fruits, as well as that which was exuded from the fragrant breasts— exceedingly sweet and most enchanting.

O you who are dear to ten thousand [beings], please accept this mortal nectar consisting of excellent cow's milk, which is endowed with a most delicious flavor and produced from the sugarcane tree. (27)

"Please accept this molasses, which is produced from powdered flour and dust, cooked by fire, and exceedingly sweet. O Goddess, please accept this sweet food consisting of well-cooked grains of barley and wheat, anointed with molasses and cow-products."
It is made from ground grains, cooked, and provided with svastikas and other auspicious marks. || 29 ||
May you accept this food offering presented by me with devotion;
it provides cool breezes and is supremely comforting during the heat. (30)
"O Kamalā, please accept this fan, this white chowrie, and this excellent, beautiful betel-leaf, well-scented with camphor and other fragrances. (31)
"Please accept this betel leaf, which removes the numbness of the tongue, is well-scented and cool, and acts as a destroyer of thirst. (32)
O Goddess, accept this life which is the very essence of the world's vitality,
the seed of divine beauty, and that which eternally increases splendor.
O Goddess, please accept this garment made of cotton and silk, as well as ornaments of red gold that enhance the beauty of the body. (34)
"O Goddess, please accept this ornament, which bestows beauty, brings fortune, is fashioned from the products of various seasons, and is the supreme abode of manifold splendor. (35)
O Goddess, please accept this pure garland, beloved by the king of the gods;
it bestows purity, possesses a pure form, and is the most auspicious of all auspicious things. (36)
O Goddess, please accept this delightful fragrance produced from fragrant substances, as well as the pure water of sacred bathing-places, which always bestows purity. (37)
"O beloved of Kṛṣṇa, please accept this beautiful water for rinsing the mouth, fashioned from the finest gems and the like, and anointed with flowers and sandalwood. (38)
"O Goddess, please accept this excellent bed, richly adorned with garments and ornaments, as well as whatever extraordinary objects exist on earth that are difficult to obtain. (39)
"O Goddess, please accept this substance which is worthy of being enjoyed as an ornament for the gods;
having offered these substances, the bull among gods was [honored] by Bhūta. (40)
Upon reaching ten lakhs, the perfection of the mantra was indeed attained. ||41||
He chanted the root mantra with devotion ten lakh times according to the prescribed rite.
Through this chanting, the mantra given by Brahmā became like a wish-fulfilling tree in every respect:
*lakṣmī-māyā-kāma-vāṇī-ṅantā-kamalavāsinī*. (42)
This Vedic king of mantras is well-known when accompanied by the word "svāhā";
by means of this mantra, Kubera attained supreme sovereignty.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter 42.
By this mantra, Dakṣa Sāvarṇi, Manu himself, and Maṅgala became lords of the earth over the seven continents as sovereigns of kings.
Priyavrata, Uttānapāda, Kedāra, and King Nṛpa—
these perfected ones and lords of kings, O Nārada, [attained success] by means of this mantra.
When the mantra was perfected, Mahālakṣmī, seated in a celestial chariot fashioned from the essence of the finest gems, appeared before Śakra to grant him a boon. 46.
Covering the earth consisting of seven islands with her radiance,
she possessed the hue of a white campaka flower and was adorned with jewel ornaments.
With a slight smile and a serene countenance, she is intent on bestowing grace upon her devotees;
she wears a jeweled necklace possessing a radiance equal to ten million moons.
Having seen the peaceful mother of the world, Purandara was filled with joy;
his entire body was covered in horripilation, his eyes were filled with tears, and he joined his palms in reverence.
And there he was joined with the King of Hymns (Stotrarāja) bestowed by Brahmā,
which is Vedic and indeed grants all desired objects.
Puraṃdara said:
Salutations to the one who dwells in the lotus, salutations again and again to Nārāyaṇī;
constant salutations again and again to Mahālakṣmī, the beloved of Kṛṣṇa. (51)
Salutations again and again to her whose eyes are like lotus petals, and salutations again and again to her named Padmā;
salutations again and again to the one seated on a lotus, to the lotus-like one, and to the consort of Viṣṇu. || 52 ||
Salutations again and again to her who is the embodiment of all prosperity and who is to be worshipped by all; salutations again and again to her who bestows devotion to Hari and who grants joy.
Salutations again and again to her who resides upon the chest of Kṛṣṇa, and to Kṛṣṇeśa;
salutations to her whose very form is the splendor of the moon, and to the beautiful jewel-lotus.
Salutations again and again to the Great Goddess, the presiding deity of prosperity;
salutations again and again to her whose nature is growth, the bestower of growth. || 55 ||
She who is Mahālakṣmī in Vaikuṇṭha, she who is Lakṣmī in the Ocean of Milk, the Lakṣmī of heaven in the abode of Indra, and the Lakṣmī of royalty in the palace of kings; 56.
She is the household fortune of householders, the domestic deity in their homes;
she was born from the ocean as Surabhi, the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) who desires the sacrifice. 57.
You are Aditi, the mother of the gods; you are Kamalā, whose abode is the lotus.
You are Svāhā in the offering of oblations, and you are remembered as Svadhā in the offering to the ancestors.
For you are indeed the Earth, whose nature is Viṣṇu, the support of all;
you are the embodiment of pure sattva, devoted solely to Nārāyaṇa.
Victorious over anger and violence, you are the bestower of boons, the auspicious Śāradā;
you are the supreme giver of the ultimate truth and the highest bestower of service to Hari.
Without her, the entire world would be reduced to ashes and rendered worthless;
without her, the whole universe would be eternally dead while yet living.
You are the supreme mother of all, appearing in the form of every kinsman;
you are the causal form of virtue, wealth, desire, and liberation.
Just as a mother is always the protector of her suckling infants during their infancy,
so too are you always the mother of all beings in every form.
One deprived of a mother may survive by chance, as does one who still nurses at the breast;
but it is certain that no person whatsoever can live if deprived of you.
O Mother, you whose very nature is supreme serenity, be gracious to me;
O Eternal One, grant me the realm seized by my enemies.
O beloved of Hari, as long as I am deprived of you, deprived of kinsmen, a mere beggar, and destitute of all prosperity, so long shall I remain thus.
Grant me knowledge and the Dharma, all desired prosperity, as well as power, majesty, and every form of authority. (67)
"Victory, prowess in battle, and supreme sovereignty as well"—
having spoken thus, Mahendra, together with all the hosts of gods, [departed].
Sādhumanetra bowed again and again with his head;
so too did Brahmā, Śaṅkara, Śeṣa, Dharma, and Keśava.
And all of them repeatedly offered exemptions for the sake of the gods; and having granted a boon to the deities, they presented a beautiful flower garland.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter 43:
Lakṣmī, being well-pleased, gave herself to Keśava in the assembly of the gods.
And the gods, being satisfied, went each to their own respective abode, O Nārada.
The goddess went to the abode of Hari after seeing him reclining upon the Ocean of Milk;
and Brahmā and Īśānī also returned to their own homes, O Nārada.
Having bestowed auspicious blessings upon the gods with affection,
a person should recite this highly meritorious hymn during the three junctions of the day.
He shall become a great lord of kings, equal to Kubera;
by merely reciting five hundred thousand times, men shall attain perfection in this hymn.
If one recites the Siddhastotra continuously for one month, he will undoubtedly become a great happy king of kings. || 75 ||
Thus ends the forty-second chapter in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa. || 42 ||
Now begins the forty-third chapter.
Nārada said:
O illustrious Nārāyaṇa, God of gods, my Lord!
By her very form, by her very virtue, by her majesty, by her splendor, and by her radiance. ||1||
O Sage, you alone are the best among the wise, the perfected ones, and the yogis; you are the supreme among ascetics and sages, and the most excellent among those who know the Vedas.
The great and wonderful narrative of Mahālakṣmī has been understood;
now, tell me some other hidden narrative. (3)
This is exceedingly secret, useful in every respect,
not to be disclosed even in the Purāṇas, declared in the Vedas, and endowed with righteousness.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O Brāhmaṇa, how many kinds of various narratives—unrevealed in the Purāṇas, profound, and very difficult to obtain—have you heard? (5)
"Among those, tell me, O illustrious one, what you wish to hear that is the most essential; afterwards, I shall explain that to you again."
Nārada said: The goddess Svāhā is praised for the offering of oblations in all rites;
Svadhā is praised for offerings to the ancestors; and Dakṣiṇā (the sacrificial fee) is the most excellent of all.
O best among the knowers of the Vedas, I desire to hear from your mouth their conduct, the fruit of their births, and their preeminence; please speak.
Sūta said:
Having heard the words of Nārada, the best of sages smiled and began to relate the ancient story as told in the Purāṇas.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: In ancient times, at the very beginning of creation, the gods went for the sake of their own sustenance;
they arrived at the world of Brahmā and reached his most enchanting assembly hall.
Having gone there, they made a request to the Sage for the sake of food;
having heard it and given his promise, Brahmā devoted himself to the worship of Śrī Hari.
Nārada said:
For the Blessed One indeed became the form of sacrifice through his own portion;
whatever oblation was given in the sacrifice by the Brahmins to those [deities], [he partook of it].
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: O best of sages, when Brahmins and others such as Kṣatriyas and so forth offer oblations, the gods do not receive that gift at all.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter forty-three.
All those gods became despondent and went again to that assembly;
having arrived, they made a report concerning the cause of their lack of food. || 14 ||
Having heard this, Brahmā took refuge in Śrī Kṛṣṇa through meditation;
by His command, he performed the worship of Prakṛti through meditation alone. (15)
By a portion of Prakṛti, she is the embodiment of all powers;
exceedingly beautiful, dark-complexioned, charming, and captivating.
With a face brightened by a slight smile and eager to bestow grace upon her devotees, she spoke thus in the presence of the Creator: "O Lotus-born One, hear my boon."
Having heard those words of his, Vidhi spoke to her in agitation.
Prajāpati said:
"O Agnihikā, become a most beautiful power. (18)
Even the fire of the sacrificial hearth is unable to burn without you;
yet, that man who shall offer oblations while uttering your name at the end of the mantra [shall succeed]. (19)
The gods receive that from the gods with great joy;
she is the mistress of the household, whose nature is the prosperity of Agni and who is the embodiment of Śrī. 20.
O Mother of the World, you are eternally worshipped by the gods, humans, and others;
yet, having heard the words of Brahmā, she became despondent.
Then the Goddess spoke her own intention to the Self-born One;
Svāhā said: "I shall worship Kṛṣṇa through austerity for a very long time."
O Brahmā, whatever else exists other than that is merely an illusion like a dream;
you are the creator of the world, and Śambhu is the all-pervading Lord who conquers death.
Śeṣa manifests as the universe, as Dharma, and as the witness of those who follow dharma;
he is the one to be worshipped before all others by the gods, and the Lord of the Gaṇas among the hosts of deities. || 24 ||
Nature (Prakṛti) is worthy of worship by all, for it was through her grace that in ancient times the sages and seers became honored by virtue of serving her.
I constantly meditate with devotion upon that lotus-foot,
calling it "the lotus-faced" and "the lotus-born," in accordance with the tradition of Padmanābha.
Having meditated upon the stainless Kṛṣṇa, the goddess, the lotus-born one, went forth for asceticism; she performed penance on one foot for a hundred thousand years.

Then she beheld Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who is beyond the qualities (nirguṇa) and transcendent of material nature (prakṛti); and having seen his exceedingly beautiful form, she herself became embodied with beauty.
In time, that woman of desire fell into a swoon before Kāmeśa;
perceiving her intention, the omniscient one spoke to her.
Having raised up that emaciated-limbed woman who had long been worn by asceticism onto his lap,
the Blessed Lord said:
"O Vārāhī, you shall indeed become my wife through a portion of yourself."
O beloved, you are the daughter of Nagnajit, known by the name Nāgnajitī;
now, O beautiful woman, you shall become the wife of Bhava and the burner of Agni.
By my grace, you shall become worthy of worship as the very form of the limbs of the mantra;
and Vahni, having worshipped you with a spirit of devotion as the mistress of his home, [shall honor you].
"She shall take delight with you, the delightful Rāmā," having spoken thus and addressed the goddess, O Nārada, the god vanished.
There, at the command of Brahmā, Vahni arrived trembling;
having meditated upon that Mother of the Universe according to the meditation prescribed in the Sāmaveda.
Having worshipped her with great satisfaction, he took her hand according to the mantras;
then, for a hundred divine years, he sported with Ramā.
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter 43:
In a place that is exceedingly secluded and always conducive to the pleasure of union.
And by the splendor of Hutāśa, a fetus was conceived within her.
That goddess bore him for twelve divine years;
thereafter, she gave birth to sons who were charming and captivating to the mind.
The Dakṣiṇāgni, Gārhapatya, and Āhavanīya fires in their proper order, as well as the sages, the ascetics, the Brāhmaṇas, the Kṣatriyas, and the others. ||38||
Having uttered the mantra ending with "svāhā," they performed the offering of the oblation;
and she who received the excellent mantra joined with "svāhā"—||39||
All success shall belong to him merely by the taking up of the mantra;
[otherwise] he is like a snake devoid of venom or a twice-born man devoid of the Vedas. || 40 ||
A woman bereft of service to her husband is like a man devoid of knowledge, or indeed like a tree stripped of its fruit and branches; she is truly censured.
Likewise, a mantra lacking its own syllables does not yield fruit when offered;
yet all the twice-born were fully satisfied, and the gods received their oblations. (42)
"By means of this very mantra ending in 'svāhā', everything indeed becomes fruitful. Thus has been told the entire, supreme narrative of Svāhā. (43)
"It bestows happiness, it bestows liberation, and it is the essence; what more do you wish to hear?
Nārada said:
"O Lord of Sages, [please tell me] the ritual for the worship of Svāhā, as well as her meditation and hymn of praise."
"O Lord, tell me that by which Vahni (Fire) worshipped and praised [him];
O Śrī Nārāyaṇa, [tell me] the meditation, the hymn of praise, and the procedure for worship as declared in the Sāmaveda. (45)
"Listen, O Brahmin, lord of sages; I shall speak of the one who destroys all sins—at the commencement of every sacrifice, [worship should be performed] either at Śālagrāma or in a water-pot. (46)
Having worshipped Svāhā with diligence, one should perform the sacrifice for the attainment of results;
she is endowed with the limbs of the mantra and is the very embodiment of mantra-siddhi.

Having meditated thus upon her as the perfected one, the bestower of success to men, and the auspicious giver of the fruits of actions, a person should offer water for the feet and other honors while reciting the root mantra. (48)
O Sage, listen: by praising [the deity] with the root mantra, "Oṃ hrīṃ svāhā to the goddess Vahnijāyā," one shall obtain all accomplishments. (49)
Whoever worships her with devotion, all their desires will surely be fulfilled.
Vahni said:
Svāhā is the beloved of Vahni, the wife of Vahni, who brings about contentment. (50)
She is power, action, the giver of time, the bringer of ripeness, and the eternal;
she is the constant movement of men, the burner, and capable of consuming all. 51.
She is the very essence of saṃsāra, yet she is the terrible one who carries one across saṃsāra;
she is the life-force of the gods and the nourisher of the body.
Whoever recites these sixteen names endowed with devotion shall attain all perfections in this world and in the next.
None of his actions shall be deficient; all his deeds will be most auspicious.
One who is childless shall obtain a son, and one who lacks a wife shall find a beloved spouse.
And having obtained his own beloved wife, who resembles Rambhā, he shall attain happiness.
Thus ends the forty-third chapter, titled "The Narrative of Svāhā," in the ninth book of the Śrī Devībhāgavata, within the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa. || 43 ||
In the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth skandha, chapter forty-three.
Now begins the forty-fourth chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Listen, O Nārada, I shall relate the excellent narrative of Svadhā.
It brings satisfaction to the ancestors and increases the fruit of the śrāddha offering. ||1||
At the beginning of creation, the Ordainer of the worlds created the hosts of ancestors—
four embodied ones and three whose nature is radiant energy.
Having seen the seven classes of ancestors, who were of pleasant form and charming,
he prepared food for them, beginning with the libations of water (tarpaṇa) and followed by the śrāddha rite.
Bathing up to the ritual libations (tarpaṇa), the ancestral rite (śrāddha), the worship of the gods,
and the daily observances (āhnika) ending with the three daily junctions (trisaṃdhyā)— these are heard in the Veda as the duties of Brahmins.
That Brahmin who does not daily perform the Śrāddha, the libation (tarpaṇa), the Bali offering, and the chanting of the Vedas at the three junctions of the day,
is like a serpent devoid of poison.
O Nārada, for one who serves not the Goddess and eats what has not been offered to Śrī Hari, his impurity lasts until his ashes; he is not worthy of any rite.
Having created the ancestral rites (śrāddha) and other ceremonies for the sake of the ancestors, Brahmā departed;
yet the ancestors do not receive them, though they are offered by the Brāhmaṇas and others.
And all of them, hungry and weary, went to the assembly hall of Brahmā;
they reported everything to him, the Ordainer of the worlds.
And Brahmā created a mind-born daughter who was enchanting, endowed with beauty and youth, and whose face resembled a hundred moons. ||9||
She was possessed of knowledge, virtuous, and endowed with exquisite beauty;
she had the luster of the color of a white campaka flower and was adorned with jewel ornaments.

She is pure, a portion of primordial nature (prakṛti), radiant with the power of ego (asmitā), bestowing boons, auspicious, named Svadhā, possessing beautiful teeth, and endowed with the marks of Lakṣmī. ||11||
She bore the lotus-feet of the ancestors placed upon her own lotus-feet;
she was the wife of the Pitṛs, lotus-faced, born from a lotus, and lotus-eyed.
Brahmā gave [this] to the Pitṛs, who were satisfied, as a form of satisfaction;
he also imparted this secret instruction to the Brāhmaṇas.
Having uttered the mantra ending with "svadhā," it was also declared that [the offering] should be given to the ancestors;
in that sequence, the brahmins in former times gave gifts to their fathers.
Svāhā is prescribed for the giving to the gods, and Svadhā is remembered for the giving to the ancestors;
in all cases, the sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) is praised, for a sacrifice without a fee is said to be destroyed.
The ancestors, the deities, the learned brahmins, the sages, and likewise the Manus, performed worship and praised Svadhā with supreme devotion and tranquility. || 16 ||
The gods and others were satisfied, their desires completely fulfilled; and the Brahmins and other ancestors were gratified by the offering of *svadhā* and divine boons.
Thus has everything been told, including the very narrative of Svadhā, which brings satisfaction to all. What more do you wish to hear?
Śrī Nārada said:

O great sage, best among the knowers of the Vedas, please speak with effort regarding the ritual for the worship of Svadhā, as well as her meditation and hymn of praise; I shall listen attentively. (19)
Nārāyaṇa said:
O Brahmin, you know everything—the meditation, the hymn of praise, the Veda, and all that is auspicious. How is it that you wish to know for the sake of further increase?
On the thirteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Śarad, under the asterism Maghā, on the day of the Śrāddha ceremony,
one should worship Svadhā with fragrant substances and then perform the Śrāddha rite.

That Brahmin who, being full of egoism, performs a *śrāddha* without first honoring his own sister will not partake of the fruit of that *śrāddha* or the libation (*tarpaṇa*); this is the truth. [He should honor] the mind-born daughter of Brahmā, who is eternally possessed of stable youth.
Worthy of worship by the ancestors and the gods, I honor her who bestows the fruit of śrāddha rites.
Having meditated thus, one should offer water for the feet (pādya) and other honors to her upon a stone slab or in an auspicious jar with the root mantra; so it is heard in the Śruti.
O great sage, [the mantra] is: "Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ svadhādevyai svāhā. Thus [it is said] in the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, in the ninth book, chapter 45.
Having recited it, worshipped it, and praised it, the twice-born man should bow down to her.
It is fearless and bestows all desires upon men; it was created in ancient times by Brahmā. ||26||
"Listen to this hymn, O best of sages, son of Brahmā.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: "By the mere utterance of the word *svadhā*, a man becomes one who has bathed in a sacred ford (*tīrtha*)."
He is liberated from all sins and obtains the fruit of the Vājapeya sacrifice. ||27||
If one should remember "Svadhā, Svadhā, Svadhā" in this manner three times,
one obtains the fruit of a Śrāddha rite as well as the offering of water (tarpaṇa) to Bali.
He who, with a concentrated mind, listens to the Svadhā-hymn at the time of the Śrāddha ceremony, shall obtain the very fruit arising from the Śrāddha; of this there is no doubt. (29)

The man who recites "Svadhā, Svadhā, Svadhā" in this manner at the three junctions of the day shall obtain a beloved, virtuous wife endowed with the qualities of a mother and possessed of offspring. (30)
You are equal to the very life-breath of the ancestors, you are the embodiment of the livelihood of the twice-born,
the presiding deity of the śrāddha rites, and the bestower of the fruits of the śrāddhas and other ceremonies.
O lady of noble vows, you are eternal and the embodiment of truth; you are the embodiment of merit.
Your manifestation and disappearance occur during creation and dissolution.
Oṃ, Svasti, Namaḥ, Svāhā, Svadhā, and likewise Dakṣiṇā—these have been designated by the four Vedas and are further praised for those engaged in ritual action. (33)
"These were created by the Lord solely for the sake of fulfilling karma"—
having spoken thus, Brahmā [resided] in his own assembly in the world of Brahmā.
And she stood there suddenly and immediately; that Svadhā manifested herself, and then she offered her very self, that lotus-faced one, to the ancestors.
Having reached her, they and their ancestors departed filled with great joy;
whoever listens with a concentrated mind to this meritorious hymn of Svadhā, [attains the same].
Having bathed in all the sacred fords, he shall obtain his desired fruit. ||36||
Thus ends the forty-fourth chapter, titled "The Narrative of Svadhā," in the ninth book of the glorious Devībhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, within the dialogue between Nārada and Nārāyaṇa. || 44 ||
Now begins the forty-fifth chapter.
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: The most excellent, sweet, and supreme narrative concerning Svāhā and Svadhā has been told.
I shall relate the narrative of Dakṣa; listen with focused attention. || 1 ||
In ancient times, in Goloka, there was a cowherd girl named Suśīlā, who was a beloved of Hari; she was a primary companion of Rādhā, blessed, venerable, and enchanting. (2)
She was exceedingly beautiful, a fortunate woman with a lovely countenance; she was learned, virtuous, possessed of supreme beauty, and a faithful wife. ||3||
Kalāvatī was of delicate limbs, lovely, and lotus-eyed; she had beautiful hips and well-formed breasts, was slender as a horse, and was rounded like a banyan tree.
Adorned with jewel ornaments, she has the luster of the color of a white *caṃpaka* flower; her lips are full and her eyes are like those of a deer. ||5||
The radiant lady, with a face slightly smiling or serene, [shone] upon Kṛṣṇa. || 6 ||
Formerly, in the presence of Rādhā, there were lovers skilled in the treatises on love, moving with the grace of swans, devoted to her inner state, and born of that very sentiment;
they were born of aesthetic rasa, connoisseurs of rasa, and eager for the rasa of Rāma, the Lord of Rāma. They sat upon his right lap.
Out of fear, Madhusūdana, seeing Rāvā before him—the most excellent among the gopīs—[acted]. ||8||
She appeared with her face cast down, her eyes red like collyrium;
her limbs trembled with anger, and her lower lip quivered in rage.
The amorous woman with a flushed face.

Beholding the lecher there, ten million and one hundred thousand gopīs became afraid; with their hands joined in *añjali*, they bowed their necks in devotion.
Saying "Protect us! Protect us!
again and again, they went for refuge at her lotus-like feet out of fear.
O Nārada, three hundred million cowherds, including Sudāmā and others, went for refuge to his lotus feet out of fear.

And it shall be reduced to ashes. || 16 ||
"From this day forward, if that Gopikā comes to Goloka, she shall perish instantly upon her arrival. Having spoken thus right there in anger, the Goddess of the lords of gods,

Not seeing Kṛṣṇa before her, Rādhā, distressed by separation and firm in her vows,

"O Kṛṣṇa, O Lord of the masters of my life, come, O you who are dearer than life!
O Lord of the gods who presides over my vital breaths, my life-breaths depart without you. (19)
A woman's pride increases day by day through her husband's good fortune; since great happiness arises from this, she should always serve him in accordance with dharma. (20)
The husband is the kinsman of noble women, their presiding deity, and their eternal refuge;
he is the very embodiment of supreme prosperity and the constant bestower of enjoyments in personified form. (21)
He who possesses pride, yet who shatters pride. ||22||

The giver of Dharma is the eternal giver of happiness, the giver of joy, and always the giver of peace; radiant with honors, he is the Master, more essential than the most essential, who increases the kinship of his relatives.
Indeed, among kinsmen, no relative is seen to be equal to a husband, the kinsman of one's kinsmen. (23)
He is called the *bhartṛ* because he supports, and the *pati* because he protects; he is the *svāmī* because he is the lord of the body, and the *kānta* because he grants desires. (24)
From the Lord of Life comes the Leader of Life. || 25 ||

A kinsman is considered dear because he increases one's happiness; a lord is dear because he bestows sovereignty; and a lover is dear because he grants pleasure—there is nothing dearer than these. A son, moreover, is born from the seed of the master; therefore, he is dear. (26)
A husband is always dearer than a hundred sons to those born of noble lineage;
however, she who is born of an ignoble family is incapable of truly knowing her beloved. 27.
It is equivalent to bathing in all sacred fords, giving sacrificial fees at all sacrifices, circumambulating the entire earth, and performing all forms of austerity. (28)
All vows and the like, whatever great gifts there are, and whatever meritorious fasts there may be—[all these are surpassed by this]. (29)
Service to the guru, service to Brahmins, and service to the Vedas— whatever such acts there may be—
are not worth even a sixteenth part of service to the feet of the Lord.
Among gurus, Brahmins, and gods, the husband is the most venerable;
to men of noble birth, the giver of knowledge is as dear as he.
Of the gopīs numbering hundreds of millions and likewise of the gopas, and of the innumerable cosmic eggs situated therein as well. ||32||
"By whose grace I am the sovereign of all things from the beginning of the universe to the end of the cosmic egg—yet I do not know that beloved one; the nature of women is difficult to overcome. (33)
Having spoken thus, Rādhikā meditated upon Kṛṣṇa there with her own devotion;
she wept out of love and cried out, "O Lord of the mistress of Rādhā! (34).
"O Beloved, grant me your sight; I am wretched and distressed by the pain of separation.
Then, O Sage, that Goddess Dakṣiṇā vanished from Goloka.
After performing austerities for a very long time, she whose body was like that of Kamalā entered [the fire].
Then all the gods and others, having performed an extremely difficult sacrifice, [departed]. (36)
They did not obtain the fruit of those [deeds]; despondent, they went to the Creator.
Having heard their report, the Creator [went] to the Lord of the World, the God of gods. (37)
He meditated with devotion for a very long time, and he received a reply.
And the Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa [arose] from the body of Mahālakṣmī. ||38||
Having extracted the mortal splendor, he gave it as a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to Brahmā;
